==Gilmore Special 2-Car Set==

[[File:2008 100% Hot Wheels 40th Anniversary Gilmore Special 2-Car Set.JPG|center|500px]]

'''White 3000 Truck'''

At the turn of the 20th century, Arthur Fremont Gilmore wanted to expand the dairy herd on his ranch in Los Angeles, so he drilled for water. To his surprise, he found oil instead. Over the next four decades, that discovery led the Gilmore family to develop an amazing company, the Gilmore Oil Company, and some of the most extraordinary promotions the oil industry has ever seen. A.F. Gimore's son, Earl Bell (E.B.) made Gimore Oil's 'Blu-Green' gas famous. E.B. built a stadium on the ranch property where midget car racing began and the season ran from May through 'Tanksgiving'. Gilmore Oil sponsored cars, boats and airplanes that set speed records. The plane's pilot was Roscoe Turner and the co-pilot was Gilmore, a small, very real lion cub.

'''Agajanian Special'''

Gilmore Oil also sponsored other cars such as Indy 500 racers, a car built to set land speed records at Bonneville, and a radio 'Circus' which featured the longest advertising jingle ever - a Gilmore Gas song which added a new verse from listeners each week. All that energetic salesmanship and the memorable 'Roar with Gilmore' series of logos promoted a chain of West-Coast Gilmore Gas stations. Today you can visit an exact replica of one of those stations, Earl's Service circa 1936, at the Original Farmers Market at Third and Fairfax in Los Angeles. It sits on the same property where a search for water created a petroleum legend.

==Mopar Muscle 2-Car Set==


'''<nowiki/>'69 Plymouth HEMI GTX'''

When the Plymouth GTX was introduced in 1967 (originally named the Belvedere), it was meant to be a "gentlemen's" muscle car - a mixture of style and performance. But there was no doubt that performance was primary if you got the model with a HEMI engine; 'Muscle' was quickly what this Plymouth was famous for. Although in its initial year only 720 were sold with the HEMI engine, the car quickly became a classic for every enthusiast.

'''<nowiki/>'69 Dodge Coronet Super Bee'''

This car is a classic for any Mopar devotee. Limited in production from 1968 to 1970, the Super Bee was an accessible, low-priced car with high-power muscle. The heavy duty suspension, optional Mopar A-833 four-speed transmission, and high performance tires were just some of the features that made this short lived production run an enduring favorite. Of course, there was also the 383hp offered in the base engine. That's muscle for your money.

This page is dedicated to the '''4-Pack'''. Mattel introduced the '''4-Pack''' in 1970 in a large white cardboard box with a window cut out. The '''4-Pack''' has four cars in either a horizonal or large blisterpack with 4 bubbles. This would include buy 3 and get one free or bonus cars.

This page is to learn more about the 4-Pack. There will not be a lot of details on the individual cars here, if there is an exception it will be in the notes in that year.

Action Machines:
The '''Hot Wheels Action Machines''' are a set of 5 [[:Category:Caterpillar Inc.|Caterpillar Construction vehicles]] which were released in 1998. They came with small container of moldable, reusable ‘Clean Dirt’ compound. They came packaged individually on a large card with unique pictures corresponding to the car.

The reverse side of the card a blueprint style artwork of the car, a small description of it and pictures of the other four cars in the series with text saying “Collect all the Action Machines vehicles to create a more powerful construction line-up for loads of fun!” 



==Clean Dirt Compound==

'''IMPORTANT''': CLEAN DIRT compound is non-toxic.

'''CLEAN DIRT COMPOUND IS NOT A FOOD PRODUCT.''' Always put CLEAN DIRT compound back in its container after use or it will dry out. If CLEAN DIRT compound dries out, work in one teaspoon of water and repeat as needed. Push down on centre of CLEAN DIRT compound lid to easily close container.

'''CAUTION: do not play with CLEAN DIRT compound on carpeting.''' CLEAN DIRT compound may stick to or stain fabrics and any varnished/unvarnished surfaces.

'''FOR BEST REMOVAL:'''

*Immediately remove excess CLEAN DIRT compound.

*On carpets, use household carpet spot remover.

*Wash with detergent and hot water; repeat if necessary

*Dry cleaning will not remove CLEAN DIRT compound

==Bulldozer==
[[CAT Bulldozer|Bulldozers]] are very powerful machines that have the tough job of clearing the landscape at a construction site. The curved blade in front pushes away heavy loads of earth and rocks. Their special crawler tracks take the place of tires and allow them to do a good job on almost any ground!

(Note: This casting is different from the ordinary [[CAT Bulldozer]] casting as it has a handle cast into the blade arm. It also uses the original casting with movable blade arm and real rubber tracks, rather than the retooled version without these features which was seen six years prior in 1992.)

50th Anniversary of Corvette 2-Car Sets:
In 2003, Hot Wheels released three 2-car sets celebrating the 50th Anniversary of Corvette. These box-sets used the '100% Hot Wheels' castings which were very detailed and featured 'Real Rider' wheels and opening hoods.

==Set 1 of 3==

[[File:DSC4707.JPG|center|500px]]
Although styling initially established the Corvette, it was the constant evolution of technology and performance that put the sports car on par with the elite Europeans. Innovation that could be described in two words - fuel injection. In 1957, an enlarged 283cid small-block engine with Ramjet fuel injection boosted 'Vette horsepower to 283. It was only the second time a Detroit V8 reached the one-horsepower-per-cubic-inch milestone. A 4-speed manual transmission also debuted that year. Performance rapidly advanced throughout the next two decades. 1982 marked the end of a body style that was envied for sixteen years but introduced an innovative drive train that included Cross-Fire fuel injection, for the next generation of Corvette body styles. 100% Hot Wheels showcases these two famous 'fuelie' models as part of the 50th anniversary celebration of America's superior sports car... the Corvette!

==Set 2 of 3==

[[File:50th Anniversary of Corvette 2 - 2-Car Set 2.JPG|center|500px]]

One of the crucial elements contributing to the success Corvette has enjoyed for 50 years is its styling. From the first model in 1953 through the current version, each body style introduced new and innovative designs that continually appealed to its consumers. This 100% Hot Wheels set features the 1953 debut model and the '96 Grand Sport, highlighted its sleek and elegant design.The C4 body styling raised the bar once again and established a new standard for America's performance icon.

The Chevrolet Corvette made its dramatic debut at the 1953 Motorama due to its eye-catching design and innovative construction. Those first 300 hand-built beauties began a fifty-year evolutionary process which has delivered five awe-inspiring body styles, and technological developments which continually satisfy the drivers highest performance expectations. This 100% Hot Wheels 50th Anniversary commemorative set, featuring models from 1957 and 1996, is a tribute to the impact and longevity of America's preeminent sports car, the Chevrolet Corvette.

30th Anniversary of '71 Muscle Cars 4-Ca:
In 2001, [[100% Hot Wheels]] celebrated the 30th Anniversary of 1971 Muscle cars by releasing this 4-Car set, featuring four brand new castings all highly detailed with rubber wheels and opening hoods.

[[File:71BoxSetFront.JPG|500px]]

In 1971, America's big three auto struggled against government safety regulations and escalating insurance premiums, but Motown's muscle cars were still popular among those who rebelled against foreign imports with four-banger engines and speedometers that barely reached three digits. Muscle cars may be on the road to becoming extinct, but they were still magnificent examples of Detroit's ability to produced technical wonders we really wanted.

After three decades we look back and savor the memories of the Ford Torino, the Dodge Charger, the Chevy Chevelle SS, and the Buick GSX, four of Motown's most muscular and magnificent machines. Now, you can celebrate them with this 100% Hot Wheels 30th Anniversary of the 1971 Muscle Cars Set.

30th Anniversary of '70 Muscle Cars 4-Ca:
In 2000, [[100% Hot Wheels]] celebrated the 30th Anniversary of 1970 Muscle cars by releasing this 4-Car set, featuring four brand new castings all highly detailed with rubber wheels and opening hoods.

[[File:70MuscleCarsBoxFront.JPG|500px]]

It was the best of times. It was the worst of times. 1970 marked the pinnacle of the great Motown muscle car era, with maximum horsepower and accelerating speeds. But sadly, it also marked the beginning of the end for these 4-speed, big block, boulevard bruisers. During the years that followed, manufacturers were plagued by safety issues, government restrictions, skyrocketing insurance premiums, and gas lines longer than drag strips - and the three big muscle car manufacturers were doomed to the fate of the dinosaurs.

Now, after three decades we look back and savor the memories of these magnificent machines and celebrate the 30th anniversary of 1970's Muscle Cars. Check 'em out.

Some of them are called trailers or campers. Others are referred to as motor homes, but there is only one company that produces "mobile mansions" known as '''Airstream'''. One of the greatest examples of 20th century industrial design, these glistening silver capsules of comfort and style have graced the roads for nearly 70 years. They are first-class coaches, manufactured from aircraft-grade aluminum, for nomadic dreamers who hit the highways expecting the creature comforts of home whether parked in the mountains, deserts or seaside. Our Airstream Dream Vehicle Set is for those nomads who relish in the thought of having the world at their doorstep, and those who live the Airstream creed, "Don't ever let your wheels stop rolling for more than 30 days at a time." 50th Anniversary Originals Series:
For the [[Hot Wheels 50th Anniversary|50th Anniversary]], Hot Wheels released several special series including the '''50th Anniversary Originals Series''' (sometimes called 'Replica Redlines'). It features five cars in [[Spectraflame]] Paint which were packaged on a card representing the original cards from 1968 and also featured a metal [[Collector's Button]]. Each car was adorned with the 50th Anniversary logo on the side. Although this series is inspired by the '[[List of 1968 Hot Wheels|Sweet 16]]' from 1968, none of the vehicles are from this era. 20th Anniversary Series:
[[File:20th_Anniversary_plate.jpg|20th anniversary plate|thumb|right|200px]] "In 1968 Mattel introduced the very first Hot Wheels vehicle. Since then millions of kids have grown up with the Hot Wheels family of cars and trucks. Now it’s our turn to say ‘thank you’ for 20 years of support! Hot Wheels is proud to present our 20th anniversary “Special Collector’s Edition” car, a sleek chrome-plated vehicle embossed with a striking 20th 20th anniversary logo! There are six different chrome-plated cars representing most of the Hot Wheels segments." (from the back of the 20th Anniversary 3 pack) For the 20th anniversary Mattel launches twelve 20th Anniversary 3 packs (thirteen if you count the variant of the pack number 6) and a 20th Anniversary gift pack with 20 cars. [[File:20th_Anniversary_engraved_logo.jpg|The striking 20th anniversary logo|thumb|right|250px]] In the 20th anniversary 3 packs you can find 23 cars from the past mainlines: 1 from 1982, 1 from 1983, 3 from 1984, 3 from 1985, 7 from 1986 and 7 from 1987; along with these ones there are two "exclusives": Thunderstreak with a color scheme that will appear in the 1989 mainline and Turbo Streak with the 20th anniversary tampo, that could be found in a rare variant of the pack 6 and in the 20th anniversary gift pack. The main course of these 20th anniversary 3 packs is the free chrome and gold vehicles embossed with a striking 20th anniversary logo. Then there is the 20th anniversary gift pack with 20 cars from the last six years: 1 from 1982, 2 from 1985, 5 from 1986, 4 from 1987 and 5 from the 1988; along with these ones there are three "exclusives": the '35 Classic Caddy with a color scheme that will appear in the 1989 mainline, Turbo Streak with the 20th anniversary tampo (here wrongfully named Thunderstreak) and the Rapid Transit (here named Team Bus) with the black windows that could be found only in this set and in the 1988 Pop 'n Play Set, school house. [[File:Hot_Wheels_20th_Anniversary_Limited_Edition_Gift_Pack_.jpg|The bizarre 20th anniversary Gift Pack|thumb|right|250px]] It seems that it's really hard to find a correct Gift Pack: the order of the vehicles isn't the one on the back card and there are some intruders. There are a gold Monster Vette and a gold Mercedes 540k (both from the 3 packs) instead of the '55 Chevy and the '37 Bugatti. 35th Anniversary of Hot Wheels 2-Car Set:
[[File:35th Anniversary of Hot Wheels 2-Car Set Deora.JPG|center|500px]] Choosing a "flagship" vehicle to commemorate the 35th Anniversary of Hot Wheels cars was not an easy task. Months of discussion took place. Heritage was an important consideration, as was power and performance. Many insisted on a cutting-edge design. The car we finally selected was a replica of a full size concept car created by former [[Hot Wheels]] designer, [[Harry Bradley]]... the [[Deora]]. It was a perfect choice because the updated [[Deora II]] released in 2000 has become popular among collectors and served as a fitting bookend to the Hot Wheels story. The Deora and the Deora II are a classic pair of California customs for those who refuse to cruise in anything but the coolest custom that can make thirty-five years go by in the blink of an eye. Action Racers:
[[File:ActionRacers.png|300px|right]]'''Action Racers''' was a series of larger-scale (approximately 1:43 scale) Hot Wheels cars produced from 1987 to about 1996, initially under the Hot Wheels Giants line. These were a series of Hot Wheels cars which featured clockwork motors which could be activated by pulling back and releasing, akin to many other clockwork toy cars. These were manufactured by [[ARCO Toys]], a subsidiary of Mattel. Numerous versions of the Action Racers were produced, each having some sort of different special trait about their paint finish. A similar series known as the [[Action Cycles]] was also produced. ==Vehicles== A number of vehicles are repeat castings but advertised under a different series. 1:43 Pull-Backs:
The '''1:43 Pull Back''' series is a larger-scale series developed by Mattel introduced in [[2022]]. This series featured pullback 1:43 scale vehicles with more detail than their 1:64 scale counterparts. These are vehicles with rubber tires and intended for kids to play with; the vehicles themselves, apart from the pullback motors, feature opening parts. All castings in this series are Hot Wheels original designs and often feature existing graphics usually found on a previous version of the casting. All castings are made in China. This series was mainly released in Asian territories, but at least one wave was available in the United Kingdom.

Adventures:
'''Adventures''' or '''Adventures with Tim & Pablo''' was a brief [[1994]] series that focused on big vehicles that would open up to transform into Playsets with miniature vehicles and buildings in order to create an adventure. The series surrounded the main Characters; Tim Taylor and his trusty dog Pablo. Each set included a Comic book, a miniature comic on the back of the blister, an image on the back of the blister setting up the adventure, an "Add-Too Adventure Map", and a message from Tim to "Stay in School. It's a Great Adventure"

Six sets with 2 Color variations with a total of 12 adventures and 1 [[McDonald's]] Happy Meal Toy, appeared in the line.

AcceleRacers (figure series):
[[File:Acceleracerslogo.jpg|center|300px]]
==Description==
The '''AcceleRacers Figure Series''' was an unreleased array of larger transformable action figures and vehicles planned for debut under the [[AcceleRacers (disambiguation)|AcceleRacers]] series in late [[List of 2006 Hot Wheels|2006]] through [[List of 2007 Hot Wheels|2007]] alongside cancelled sequels 5-8 of the [[Hot Wheels: AcceleRacers (film series)|''Hot Wheels: AcceleRacers'']] film series. Models were defined as "Mid-Scale" in patent descriptions<ref>[https://patents.google.com/patent/US7722426B2 Reconfigurable toy extreme sport hang glider - Pat. US7722426B2]</ref> <ref> [https://patents.google.com/patent/US7722429B2 Transformation toy and related products - Pat. US7722429B2]</ref> <ref>[https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/bb/81/12/81e87718894d0c/US8337271.pdf Reconfigurable toy - Pat. US8337271B2]</ref> <ref>[https://www.google.com/patents/USD540890 Reconfigurable toy dragonfly vehicle - Pat. USD540890]</ref> though no standard or metric conversion was listed. It was stated that multiple members of the [[Design Team]] travelled to Japan for a conference with designers of [[Takara Tomy]] due to their experience with transformable toy mechanisms. Early prototypes were revealed at the [[San Diego Comic-Con Exclusive Cars|San Diego Comic-Con]] event (exhibit lot #3029, booth #3445) from July 14, 2005 to July 17, 2005. Figures and accessories from the Ride-On and Character subset would have had two variants each; many of the names for releases of this series were not finalized. Designs and concepts of this series were later adapted and used in [[Stunt Strikers]] and [[Battle Force 5 (disambiguation)|Battle Force 5]].

Action Duos:
==Description==
The '''Action Duos''' series first debuted under The Dark Knight subset of the [[DC Comics]] license in [[List of 2008 Hot Wheels|2008]]. Each set consisted of a single-lane rubber band launcher that could be slotted over a length of track and two models. The launcher style of this assortment was later modified for [[Battle Pack]] releases under the [[Battle Force 5]] series in [[List of 2009 Hot Wheels|2009]].

'''Battle Force 5''' (conceptualized as '''BattleRacers''') was a series that debuted in late [[2009]] through [[2010]] to coincide with the ''[[Hot Wheels: Battle Force 5]]'' television series of the same name. It consisted of fifteen released new models and variations (twenty-two or more planned) and two Special Edition subsets (three or more planned) each containing one, two, or no attachable weapon accessories. Many products of this series went unreleased due to a combination of poor sales and marketing.

Black Convertible Collection:
The '''Black Convertible Collection''' is a book-like boxed 8-piece set that was only available in Target department stores in 1996. The set included exactly what the name implies: eight convertibles, painted in Metalflake Black. All have a Black interior, Black tinted windows, and Black tinted wheels.  Made in Malaysia, Toy #15171.

==Auto Milestones Description==
Released in 2002 only, the '''Auto Milestones''' featured 16 classic automobiles that redefined history.

This series was exclusive to [[Wal-Mart]].

All but 2 featured Real Rider tires and special tampo's saying " Automobile Milestones 2002".  On the back of the blisterpack it describes the Vision and conviction by imaginative minds to build these better automobiles.  It goes on to explain how each of these castings/automobiles changed the history of automobiles.

Attack Pack:
[[File:Attackpacktitle.gif|200px|right]]'''Attack Pack''' was a series of monstrous trucks and vehicles designed by [[Mike McKittrick]], [[Wayne Halford]], [[Keith Hippely]], [[Gary Swisher]], [[Terry Choy]], [[Kevin Gray]], [[Phil Riehlman]], and many others released from [[1992]] to [[1994]]. The main gimmick of these vehicles was their transforming action when they were pressed down, causing them to open their mouths or perform other actions. They were even available as McDonalds Happy Meal toys, as an option to Barbie dolls. Several of the Attack Pack vehicles are easy to identify, since they are marked "Attack Pack", and some even "Hot Wheels" and also have a round symbol (except for the original series of cars and the repaints of those, and the Big Ones and Biggest Ones) with a hand doing a thumbs up or a scary face with fangs, representing the Heroic Cat Pack and Evil Rat Pack respectively. The series was later succeeded by the [[Road Beasts]] line. ==Narrative== The series focuses on two teams in a rainforest, the Heroic Cat Pack and the Evil Rat Pack, who aim to get a newly-discovered energy source promising clean and safe energy for all. Focusing on Capt. Bob Catxel, nicknamed "Slash", he sets out to preserve the rainforest with his team and thwarting the efforts of the Evil Rat Pack, led by Rip, who aim to destroy it to get the energy source. Both teams are subsequently attacked by a mysterious group of beasts, giving both of them the powers of "molecule morphing", allowing vehicles to transform into animal-vehicle hybrids, featuring the "strength of the beasts", "power of their trucks" and "the intelligence of man". The teams are assisted by the "Big Ones" and the "Biggest Ones", significantly larger underlings working under Slash and Rip, as well as the Growlers, other underlings used for intimidation. Some time later, both teams enlist the help of the Battle Birds, aircraft also endowed with the "molecule morph" abilities, aiding both teams in their pursuit of the energy source. Soon after, a number of unidentified flying objects also seeking this energy source are also endowed with these "molecule morph" abilities and crash land in the rainforest; both teams find these objects and reprogram them for their purpose, and they are christened Alien Invaders. The Alien Invaders allied with the Heroic Cat Pack are programmed to defend the stratosphere from rogue alien attacks, while the Alien Invaders allied with the Evil Rat Pack are programmed to burn the ozone layer, in theory razing the rainforest and making it easier for them to find the energy source. The fighting by the Heroic Cat Pack and Evil Rat Pack subsequently disrupts a forcefield in an "ancient, undiscovered area" of the rainforest, altering the environment permanently and resulting in large military vehicles which are part dinosaur. These are subsequently recruited by both packs to assist in their efforts. An additional three vehicles, consisting of two standard Attack Pack members and one Growler, each join the team for their efforts in addition to the dinosaurs. ==Products== ===Attack Pack=== '''BIRTH OF THE ATTACK PACK'''

While in the forest, giant beasts attack the two teams and perform a "molecule morph" – melding man, machine and monster into one. Basic Pro Racing Series:
==Description==
When the premium [[1997 Pro Racing|Pro Racing]] series debuted in 1997, this basic series was also issued to supplement it. Cars in this series featured a few cost saving measures compared to more expensive alternative, such as plastic wheels and bases, and a few less details. While the Premium castings where made for display purposes, the Basic line was meant for the track. This series was also used for commemorative blisters, baggie promos, and even [[MLB Team Promotions]] until the mid 2000s.

== Basic Pro Racing 2002==
"NASCAR races are a total-body experience: when forty-three 700-horsepower engines roar by, you feel it in your bones. Grandstands rumble as these racers thunder past, the smell of burnt rubber hangs in the air, and the roar of the engines hits like waves on a beach. Hot Wheels Racing brings home the excitement of the track with the 2002 series of 1:64 scale NASCAR models. Featuring authentic team colors and logos on die-cast bodies, these highly-detailed cars are sure to be a hit with NASCAR fans. The most hard-charging NASCAR teams are available in incredible detail — look for your favorite drivers and add them to your collection!"

[[file:Autocity logo large.jpg|center|300px]] ==Description== '''Auto-City''' is an international series that first debuted in [[1994]]. It consisted of models previously used by [[Corgi Toys]] packaged or [[Retool|retooled]] with a Corgi or [[Hot Wheels]] logo on their [[baseplates]] after [[Mattel]] acquired the brand and assets. Factories were moved from Great Britain to China. This series was commonly available in Europe, Canada, Australia, and many other countries outside the United States. Castings that debuted in this series went on to be used in [[Auto-City Action Squad]], [[Hot Wheels World]], and many other series. An adapter was later made to connect Auto-City playsets to the [[Street Traxx]] system and was available by mail-in. ''Included on this page will '''only''' be the “Hot Wheels Auto-City” (1994) packaging variations.'' ''Some of these castings never received names from Hot Wheels. Names given by [[Corgi Toys]] will be used to refer to these models.'' ''Two lines of 1:43 scale Corgi models were later released under Hot Wheels branding. For information on those lines, see [[Corgi Collection]] (1995) and [[Turbos Collection]] (1996). Batman Shields Up 2-Car Set:
[[File:Batmobile_2004_and_Shields_Up.jpg|500px]]

As a sleek roadster, the Batmobile is unstoppable on the tough terrain of Gotham City. Designed to handle razor-sharp turns at blinding speeds, the vehicle can accelerate from 0 to 90 mph in mere seconds, catching any adversary foolish enough to escape.

But in the heat of battle, the Batmobile is ready to rumble as a full-force armored vehicle. Batman's voice-activated controls transform his racing machine into central command, providing him all the protection needed to complete his mission. Armed with everything from axle grenades to bullet-proof plating, there is no doubt Batman drives the hottest wheels in town!

We are proud to present the 1:64 scale Batmobile and the vehicle in its transformed state in this collectible 2-car set.

America's Most Beautiful Roadster (AMBR):
In the world of hot rods and custom cars, to win the AMBR at Oakland is the equivalent of winning 'Best In Show' at the Pebble Beach Concourse d'Elegance for a classic car owner. Indeed, the nine-foot tall trophy bestowed upon the winner of annual America's Most Beautiful Roadsters award is impressive in size, grandeur and importance. For 52 years, the majestic prize has been bestowed upon the most talented people within the rod and custom car culture.

Our custom car set celebrates the immeasurable talents of two AMBR honorees, both ingenious designers and creators of magnificent machines; George Barris and his "Ala Kart" and Chip Foose's "0032" created for Chuck Svates. Their vehicles are two big-time winners in 1:64 scale.

Baur's Beasts 2-Car Set:
[[File:Baurs Beast Promo Website.jpg|thumb]]
Produced in 1999, made in China.  Toy #23206.

The one thing that will ''never'' be said about [[Bruce Baur|Bruce Baur's]] vehicles is that they are under-powered! Amongst Hot Wheels designers Bruce is the one keenly focused on cylinders, valves, overhead cams and super-chargers. In fact, the horsepower produced by Baur's Beasts would total over 9000 ponies. Bruce might have to buy a gas station to feed his beasts. Check 'em out!

==Go-Mad==
This Chevy Nomad with a chopped top and a way-altered wheelbase, is a quarter-mile asphalt burner boasting four - count 'em - four Hemi engines, each of which could be capable of producing 1500 horsepower. Yikes! Can you say smoke 'em.

==Torqued Off==
Bruce's customized super semi-truck boats two Allison aircraft engines, each of which would produce 3000 horsepower and torque that would go off the charts. Massive side scoops were designed to suck up air and help cool these hyper-hot twin-gines. This sure-to-be-fast beastie brings a new meaning to the term car-go!

Anniversary Series:
====Golden Anniversary====
In 2018, Hot Wheels celebrated its 50th Anniversary. To celebrate its Golden Anniversary, they released the 50th Anniversary Black & Gold Collection, a series of 6 cars and 1 chase model painted in satin black with gold accents. Each year a different collection was released to celebrate the age of the brand. While the word "Anniversary" was removed from the title of the series, each set was easily identified by its distinctive color theme and anniversary number printed on each car. 

#2018 [[50th Anniversary Black and Gold Series (2018)|50th Anniversary Black & Gold Series]] - 6 cars and 1 chase model
#2019 [[Satin and Chrome Series (2019)|51st Anniversary (Satin & Chrome Series)]] - 6 cars and 1 chase model


==== Pearl & Chrome====
By 2020, the series had been internally named "Pearl and Chrome", identifying the primary and accent colors. This name has has since been used to identify the series and can be found on product packaging and their marketing. Further changes for the Pearl and Chrome Anniversary releases include 2 mixes of 5 or 6 seasonal releases, with 1 to 2 chase models depending on the series. For 2023 there is one chase car in each case.

#2020 [[Pearl and Chrome Series (2020)|52nd Anniversary (Pearl & Chrome Series)]] - 6 cars and 1 chase model
#2021 [[Orange and Blue Series (2021)|53rd Anniversary (Orange and Blue Series)]] - 2 mixes - 10 cars and 1 chase model
#2022 [[Blue and Pink Series (2022)|54th Anniversary (Blue and Pink Series)]] - 2 mixes - 10 cars and 1 chase model

#2024 [[Green and Gold Series (2024)|56th Anniversary (Green and Gold Series)]] - 2 mixes - 10 cars and 2 chase models
#2025 [[Purple and Gold Series (2025)|57th Anniversary (Purple and Gold Series)]] - 2 mixes - 10 cars and 2 chase models

Ballistiks:
[[File:Ballistics Logo.png|right|200x200px]]
'''Ballistiks''' was a short-lived series of "compressible" plastic Hot Wheels cars produced from 2012 to 2013; these were packaged in blister packs and could be tried in-package with a pull tab. The cars in said series could transform into balls for storage and worked in various playsets. Later cars were released under the '''Ballistiks: Full Force''' branding. [[Dave Sheltman]] and [[Kevin Cao]] were involved with this series, as well as a Gustavo Ferreyra. The series did not appear to be popular and was discontinued after a year.

Apollo Mission Action Pack:
'''Apollo Mission''' was an [[Action Packs|Action Pack]] released in 1998. It contains models of the Lunar Roving Vehicle and Lunar Module of the Apollo 15 Mission which took place on July-August 1971. It also contains figurines of Commander [[wikipedia:David Scott|David Scott]] and Lunar Module Pilot [[wikipedia:James Irwin|James Irwin]] (neither are named on the packaging), their tools and a flag of the United States of America. [[File:1998AP-ApolloMission (1) (Large).JPG|500px]] ==Description== '''FIRST WHEELS ON THE MOON!'''
Apollo 15 was the 4th manned lunar landing mission and the first to bring along a set of wheels in the form of a Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV). The electric powered vehicle weighed about 460 lbs. and had a blazing top speed of 8 mph. ==Vehicles== The following vehicles were included in the '''Apollo Mission Action Pack''': {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size: 85%; text-align: left;" width="55%" ! style="border-style: none none solid solid" |'''Casting Name''' ! style="border-style: none none solid solid" |'''Color''' ! style="border-style: none none solid solid" |'''Photo''' |- |[[Lunar Roving Vehicle]] |Silver and Copper |[[File:1998AP-ApolloMission (4) (Large).JPG|center|75px]] |- |[[Lunar Module]] |Gold and Gray |[[File:1998AP-ApolloMission (5) (Large).JPG|center|75px]] |} ==Gallery== 1998AP-ApolloMission (3) (Large).JPG 1998AP-ApolloMission (2) (Large).JPG ==Notes== *This was the only use of both vehicles. Battle X:
[[File:BattleX.png|right|200px]]'''Battle X''' was a short-lived series of battery-powered battling toys produced in [[2005]].

The premise of this series is similar to that of a cross between ''[[wikipedia:Beyblade|Beyblade]]'' and ''[[wikipedia:BattleBots|BattleBots]]'' or ''[[wikipedia:Robot Wars|Robot Wars]]'', where vehicles battle each other in a spinning fashion. Each vehicle consists of a shield piece and a spinning weapon piece; the shield is attached onto the weapon. Each vehicle takes 2 "AA"-sized batteries.

To play, both vehicles are hooked together using their hook mechanisms and are turned on simultaneously using the power switches on the right hand side of their body. Once they are powered, the vehicles will spin around in a counterclockwise fashion as they come closer to each other; the winner is the vehicle with its parts remaining by the end of the battle. The vehicle with no parts left will be bricked with its spoiler kicked downwards, propping the vehicle up. Winning a battle allows a player to attach a "Battle Scar" sticker to their vehicle.

Each vehicle can be augmented with different weapons: Blades, Extenders, Missiles and Grinders, which can be attached in place of their standard weapons. These vehicles are available in different weapons packs with two different weapons inside. 2-Packs of vehicles are also available.

American Flyer:
[[File:AmericanFlyerlogo.png|center|300px]]
==Description==
'''American Flyer''' is an American company specializing in S-gauge trains, currently existing in name only as [[Lionel|Lionel, LLC]]'s brand name for their S-gauge offerings. The origins of the brand date back to 1906, where Illinois-based toymaker William Hafner and his friend and business partner William Coleman began producing toy trains for the Edmonds-Metzel Hardware Company using the company's excess manufacturing capability; the name "American Flyer" was adopted in 1908. The company was acquired by the [[Lionel, LLC|Lionel Corporation]] in 1967.

Today the American Flyer name is used for Lionel's S-gauge semi-scale offerings, using similar technology to what is used on their [[LionChief]], Ready-to-Run and [[Ready-to-Play]] products. A sub-series was planned in [[2019]] to commemorate the 50th anniversary of [[Hot Wheels]]. One known product was planned for this series but was not released as the product failed to meet Lionel's minimum order quantities in order for it to be produced; it is not known if other products were conceptualized.

Classics:
Hot Wheels Classics was a line of vehicles released between 1987 and 1989, and is not to be confused with Mattel's later line called [[Hot Wheels Classics]]. The Classics line featured mostly cars from the 1920's through the 1950's and included such vehicles as [['37 Bugatti]] and [[Talbot Lago]] and street rods such as [[T-Bucket]] and [['32 Ford Delivery]]. The special cards for this line featured a [[Rolls-Royce Phantom II]].

=Bonus Cars=
The Mattel Bonus car program began in 1995 along with the popular [[Segment Series]] of cars.

The [[Bonus Cars]], also later called [[Mystery Cars]] (not to be confused with peg hanging black opaque blister packs) were obtained only through mail order.  The requirement was to purchase the complete segment series of cars and send the backing cards to Mattel.  In return you received one of the exclusively decorated cars .

{|border="0" cellspacing="1" cellpadding="1"
|[[File:Bodyswappers package.jpg|250px]]
|The Body Swappers Gift Pack featured vehicles with interchangable bodies. The package included 3 bodies, 3 chassis, and a plastic wrench for unlocking the bodies from the chassis. The red sports car also featured a removable chrome engine for when mated with the sporty chassis. A knockoff of this product that was made in Hungary using the same cars (but with different color schemes) and socket wrench system also existed.

The castings where later used without authorization for the Hungarian toy line; [https://t-hunted.blogspot.com/2025/11/metal-play-mobil-hungria.html Metal Play Mobil].
|[[File:Bodyswappers_set.JPG|250px]]

Cap Blastin':
[[File:Cap Blastin.JPG|left|thumb|150px|Front of the Package]][[File:Cap Blastin Back.JPG|right|thumb|150px|Back of the Package revealing a Blue Prototype [[Road Pirate|Blast Trax]]]]
'''Cap Blastin' Hot Wheels''' were a series released in 1991. Each car was packaged with a launcher and percussion caps. Even though there is six cars in this series only three different castings were used. '''Back Burner''' & '''Sonic Special''' are the same casting which was later released as [[Speed Blaster]]. '''Jet Threat''' & '''Blast Trax''' are also the same casting which was later released as [[Road Pirate]]. Lastly, '''[[Velocitor (Cap Blastin')|Velocitor]]''' & '''Road Torch''' are the same casting that appears to have not been released again. However, the names '''Velocitor''' & '''Road Torch''' were recycled for other castings.

Notice the names of each car is a re-issued name from somewhere in the Mattel lineup of toys. Usually this happens when a name needs to have copyrights renewed. "Back Burner" a 1986 Science Friction casting from the Ultra Hots lineup. "Jet Threat" the original redline car to the blackwall era. "Velocitor" was a new name but, re-copyrighted again into the Thunderburner of the late 90's. "Sonic Special" was originally the Mini Truck of 1990's. "Blast Trax" This must be a new name and no reference's to past products in HW. "Road Torch" used again based off the Mercedes race car from the mid-80s. Still to this day names are reused to be saved by copyright renewals

Character Cars:
[[File:CharacterCars.png|200px|right]]'''Character Cars''' is a series of Hot Wheels cars in production from [[2010]] to [[2024]]. These are representations of famous characters in television shows, movies and other forms of media as cars. The series was conceived in 2010 by [[Jun Imai]] and [[Kevin Cao]], with the first depictions being of characters from ''[[Toy Story Character Cars|Toy Story]]''. This series was discontinued in [[2024]] and replaced by [[Hot Wheels RacerVerse]].

Classic Bodies 2-Car Set:
[[File:1_Type_57C_Bugatti_Cabriolet_and_1932JS_Duesenberg.JPG|500px]]

These two exquisite vehicles would draw center stage attention at any Concourse d'Elegance! Very few Duesenbergs and Bugattis were ever produced - fewer exist today - making them highly desirable, and commanding prices that begin in seven figures.

100% Hot Wheels presents our Classic Bodies vehicle set featuring models of one-of-a-kind roadsters with rich histories - but not rich price tags. The [['32 Duesenberg SJ|1932/JS Duesenberg]] was custom-built on two continents for the Maharajah of Jahore, one of India's riches princes. The straight-8 320 bhp engine was capable of hitting 120 mph and featured a classic hood, streamline boat tail and rumble seat. It is truly a masterpiece fit for a Maharajah!

The French government presented the French-built [[Type 57C Bugatti Cabriolet]] to the Shah of Iran on the occasion of his marriage, in 1939. It is considered by many to be the most elegant of sophisticated body styles ever conceived.

Bruce Meyer Gallery 4-Car Set:
[[File:BRUCE_MEYER_GALLERY_1.JPG|500px]]

Growing up in southern California, Bruce Meyer fell in love with cars at an early age. Sports cars were his passion; Porsches and Cobras specifically, but then his taste broadened to include classic cars, then hot rods and racecars. Before he knew it, Bruce had accumulated a small fleet of vehicles. His gallery is possibly the finest private collection of historically accurate cars in the country. Bruce is widely admired and respected within the automotive community for his knowledge and contributions and is Chairman of the Board of the Petersen Automotive Museum.

100% Hot Wheels is proud to offer these historically significant vehicles in its Bruce Meyer Gallery.

Don Prudhomme's reputation as "The Snake" was established in this 'Greer/Black/Prudhomme' full-body dragster. The Snake won an amazing 137 of 141 races behind its wheel and went on to become the winningest driver of the early '60's.

The Pierson Brothers '34 Ford 3-window coupe is widely considered the most famous coupe in hot rod history. Brothers Dick and Bob built this record holding red to be run on dry lakes. It continuously set top speed records from the '50's through the '90's.

The So-Cal Belly Tank was a unique dry lake racer that was constructed from a P-38 fighter plane's fuel tank. It was a world-record holder at 198 MPH and won awards for its sleek good looks as well. It is an icon for the world of speed.

The Agajanian Special won the 1952 Indianapolis 500 driven by 22-year-old Troy Rutmann, the youngest driver in history to win the 500. It was the last 'dirt' car to win the 500 mile race marking an end of an era. #98 is remembered and revered for its style and significance.

Classical Gassers 2-Car Set:
[[File:ClassicalGassers3.JPG|500px]]

Our Classical Gassers car set celebrates two of the gasser wars' more famous and able combatants.

John Mazmanian's supercharged Austin gas coupe with its chopped top and sloped back was aptly named "The Football" after its radical shape. In 1967 the Austin ran 161.87 MPH at 8.68 seconds and went on to win many match races and AA/GS programs in California.

George "Honker" Striegel of Clay Smith Cams owned and raced this Henry J, utilizing his technical expertise in manufacturing high performance equipment to get every bit of horsepower out of the classic Kaiser.

Together, these two vehicles have burned lasting memories in the hearts and minds of A/GS and AA/GS fans across the country.

Carroll Shelby Cobra 2-Car Set:
[[File:CarrollShelbyCobraSetBoxFront.JPG|500px]]

No other racecar driver, designer and builder has had such a powerful influence on the history of the sports car than Carroll Shelby. Nurturing the idea of developing an inexpensive American sports car, Shelby designed a vehicle with a light sports car chassis, powered by an American V8 engine. Known as the Cobra, his car set the tone for the '60's Muscle Car era and became an instant legend.

With the introduction of his new Series 1 sports car, Carroll Shelby continued his tradition of creating vehicles possessing undeniable charisma and all-but-unbeatable performance. We are proud to honor Carroll Shelby and salute his immeasurable impact on the automotive industry through the design, engineering and building of legendary Shelby sports cars.

Car Craft Magazine 2-Car Set:
During the '50s and '60s, Detroit's legendary Woodward Avenue was the "unofficial" test track for the owners of Motown's most muscular cars. Technology would roll off the assembly lines and right onto the streets, where gear heads would cruise on summer nights, looking for the next quarter mile challenge, or for the prettiest girl at the hamburger stand. Well, those good ol' days are back! Since its inception in 1995, the organizers of the Woodward Avenue Dream Cruise have invited custom car and hot rod owners - and their fans - to a trip back in time by returning to the scene of their youth. The response has been overwhelming! Last summer, several hundred thousand enthusiasts traveled to Detroit for this annual weekend-long celebration of automotive dreams. Color Reveal:
[[File:ColorReveal.png|200px|right]]'''Color Reveal''' is a sub-series of the [[Color Shifters]] series. The castings in this series are essentially Alternative versions of regular Color Shifters castings but are coated in a coat of water-soluble paint. When initially dipped in water and swirled around, the water-soluble paint coat of the casting dissolves; after the paint coat dissolves the casting acts like any regular Color Shifters casting. The paint coat application is often noted to be poorly done. The castings are packaged in a barrel drum sealed in a plastic bag; the barrel drum contains a foldable hang tab. Each package contains two castings. The drum may also function as a dunk tank as well as car storage. Bondy Fiesta Candy Container Cars:
{{stub}}
'''Bondy Fiesta Candy Container Cars''' are a series of of large scale all plastic cars filled with candy made by Bondy Fiesta only for Mexico. They all use pre-existing mainline designs, including: [[Vulture]], [[Sinistra]], [[Sling Shot]], [[Side Draft]], [[Pony Up]], and [[40 Somethin']]. The US got a version of the same cars in 2005, see [[Frankford Candy Container Cars]] for those. Unlike the US versions the Mexican versions come in blister packs. They may have not been in production consistently since 2004, as the first (archived) product listing of them on the company's website is from [https://web.archive.org/web/20171113172711/http://bondyfiesta.com:80/catalogo/categoria/hot-wheels.html November 2017], however the archive only goes back to 2015. They may still be produced, the product is still listed as of 2023 but is unavailable for purchase.

Designers Challenge:
[[File:Logo-Designers.jpg|200px|right]] This series was released in 2008. For this series, Mattel went outside the company and got designers from automakers Ford, Mitsubishi, Chrysler (Dodge), Lotus, Honda, and GM (Chevrolet) to design a Hot Wheels casting. Hot Wheels designer [[Jun Imai]] designed the last casting in the series, HW40. All were made in Thailand. From the back of the cards: '''Designer's Challenge™'''
The Designer's Challenge™ program was created as a way for Hot Wheels® to actively include its automotive partners in its 40th anniversary celebration by creating exclusive designs for a brand new line. It marks the first time Mattel has ever turned outside the company for original Hot Wheels® designs. The challenge for each automotive manufacturer was to create a Hot Wheels® car that truly captured the brand's core values of speed, power, performance and attitude, while also retaining the distinct attributes of each company's brand essence. All submissions were judged by a panel of Hot Wheels® designers and collectors, as well as automotive journalists from ''Car & Driver'' magazine, the ''Los Angeles Times'' and ''Men's Journal''. The panel selected one design from each manufacturer and one internal design to be transformed into authentic Hot Wheels® cars. Connect Cars:
[[File:Connectcars.jpg|200px|right]]
Connect Cars are a series of cars that come with interlocking display cases.
[[File:Connect_Cars_01.jpg|center|500x500px]]

==50 States==
There are 50 cars representing 50 States numbered in the order they join the union. There is also an additional car to represent Washington DC. All cars were picked very carefully by Hot Wheels Designers to try to capture that particular state’s essence. In order to get the Exclusive Washington D.C. Car, you must purchase 20 Connect Cars at a retailer then send in by mail purchase. Valid through 01/14/2009 - 11/30/2009. Go to www.HotWheelsCollector.com for the order form and full details.

Demolition Man:
[[File:Demolition Man Logo.JPG|center|500px]] In 1993 Hot Wheels came out with a series of cars for the movie '''''[[wikipedia:Demolition Man|Demolition Man]]'''''. The cars in the series came packaged with a "Cryo Cube". The plastic interlocking cubes are the same as the [[Park 'n Plates]] boxes but have flat plastic covers with a paper picture of the real car from the movie instead of the license plate like covers. There were nine cars in the series, but only seven were actually new; some of the castings in this series did not actually appear in the movie or acted as stand-ins for ones that did. A notable quirk about the new castings in this series is that all feature "''''93 Warner'''" on their bases; this is copyright info related to Warner Bros., the distributors of the film. In later releases of the castings, this copyright is scrubbed off and replaced with generic "'93 Mattel" copyright information, along with the names of the cars ("Aurora" for the Oldsmobile Aurora, 442 for the Olds 442 etc.). Another notable quirk is that some of the cars in this series do not feature any interiors, with painted pieces of the body masquerading as windows or windshields; it is not clear why this was done, although one theory was that the designers were not confident with making a profit off this series and kept production costs to a minimum. ===Vehicles=== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size: 100%; text-align: left" width="100%" ! style="border-style: none none solid solid" |'''Toy #''' ! style="border-style: none none solid solid" |'''Casting''' ! style="border-style: none none solid solid" |'''Color''' ! style="border-style: none none solid solid" |'''Wheel Type''' ! style="border-style: none none solid solid" |'''Photo Loose''' ! style="border-style: none none solid solid" |'''Photo Carded''' |- |10566 |[[Oldsmobile Aurora]] |Metalflake Gray |[[BW]] |[[Image:Oldsmobile Aurora Gry.JPG|100px|center]] |[[Image:Demolition Man 1993 Oldsmobile Aurora Malaysia 10566.jpg|100px|center]] |- |11082 |[[Olds 442 W-30]] |Red |[[BW]] |[[Image:Olds 442 W-30 Red.JPG|100px|center]] |[[Image:Demolition Man 1993 Olds 442 W-30 Malaysia 11082.jpg|100px|center]] |- |11083 |[[GM Ultralite]] |White & Black |[[UH]] |[[Image:GM Ultralite Deman.JPG|100px|center]] |[[Image:Demolition Man 1993 GM Ultralite Malaysia 11083.jpg|100px|center]] |- |11084 |[[GM Lean Machine]] |Metalflake Gray |[[UH]] & [[MC1]] | [[Image:GM Lean Machine Demo.JPG|100px|center]] |[[Image:Demolition Man 1993 GM Lean Machine Malaysia 11084.jpg|100px|center]] |- |11085 |[[Corvette Stingray III|Corvette Sting Ray III]] |Dark Red |[[PC5]] |[[Image:Corvette Stingray III - Dragstrip Demons:
[[File:DragstripDemonslogo.png|200px|right]]
This article is a list of vehicles from the '''Dragstrip Demons''' released in 2009 and 2010. Over the series' two year duration, 55 different cars were released, all with a metal base, Real Rider wheels and detailed decoration, with most cars mimicking real-life drag cars. For this series, 18 different castings were used with 13 of them brand-new never-before-seen.

The Dragstrip Demons Series was replaced by [[Vintage Racing Series (2011)|Vintage Racing]] in 2011.

In 2018, a segment of the Car Culture Series was named 'Dragstrip Demons' which used the original logo.

==Description==
Crack-Ups was a line of Hot Wheels that was produced from 1985 to 1987. The castings' main feature was a revolving panel that when "crashed" spin around to show a large simulated dent on a specific part of the vehicle.

Heading titles are for '''reference only'''. They are not official casting names.

Computer Cars Series:
[[File:Computercars.jpg|200px|right]] Computer Cars, released in 1996, were six models that each came with a 3.5-inch floppy disc unique to that model. The disc included collectors facts, a comic strip and a mini-game. As of March 2019, the data off of the floppy disks of all 6 cars are available to [https://vetusware.com/manufacturer/Mattel%20Interactive/?author=57 download from Vetusware.] As of October and November 2019, YouTube user 77Pacer has published 6 videos showcasing the programs of the Computer Cars, one video for each program. All were made in Malaysia. NOTE: There are a few differences between the cars shown in the programs and the actual cars that came in the blister package. While the Oscar Mayer Wienermobile, '96 Mustang and Hydroplane appear to be the same as the final production Hot Wheels cars that came in the blister packages, that's not the case with '93 Camaro, Rigor Motor and Power Pistons. '93 Camaro is shown in the program with red wheels in the front and white wheels in the back (complete with Goodyear tampos on the tires, perfectly matching the race car driven by Jack Baldwin in 1992), but some time after the game was completed, this was changed to the 5-Spoke ([[5SP]]) wheels on the final production version. Rigor Motor originally had the Black Wall ([[BW]]) wheels and the chrome on the engine was originally light gold at the time it was photographed for the Rigor Motor program, but this was later changed to the 5-Spoke wheels and Green Chrome of the final production version. Power Pistons originally had the 5-Spoke Wheels during its program photography, but these were swapped out for the Pro Circuit 6-Spoke ([[PC6]]) wheels of the final version. '''Hot Wheels Cool Classics''' was first released in 2013. They are marketed towards adult collectors and were priced around $3.99 ([[Wikipedia:United States Dollar|USD]]). Each car features a metal base, [[Spectrafrost]] colors, and [[RSW|Retro Slot Wheels]].  All were made in Thailand.

==Hot Wheels Cool Classics 2013==
2013 card has a silver background behind the vehicle, and features the [[Custom Otto]] artwork in either blue or red.  All models came with both [[Custom Otto]] color variants on the card.

Custom Classics:
[[File:CustomClassics-logo.jpg|200px|right]]The '''Custom Classics''' line was first released in 2007. The line featured models in the 1/50 scale that were highly detailed. All models came with rubber wheels that had treads. The reason this line didn't run very long is probably the over-use of some castings. Some cars were used eight times in one year. Sometimes even multiple times in a series.

"Custom Classics™ bring custom hot rods to the next level. They get there with the latest features like custom rims and airbag suspensions. Our versions of the cult favorites all ride just right with a low-down stance and eye-popping paint jobs."

Corvette Showcase 45th Anniversary 2-Car:
In 1998, Hot Wheels released a pair of 2-Car sets to commemorate the 45th Anniversary of Corvette. They each featured two brand new Corvette castings from the collector-aimed 100% Line, all featuring opening hoods.

Dream Car (drem kar) adj. 1. An automobile that performs to the highest expectations of its driver. 2. Psychology. A vehicle inspiring mental images, emotions and sensations so gratifying they create a sense of longing. see: CORVETTE.

GM's 2-Seater made its dramatic and successful debut at the 1953 Motorama due to its eye-catching design and innovative construction. From those first 300 Polo White, hand-built beatuies of '53 evolved the powerful, 430 horsepower, '67 Stingray, then the shark-like body style of the '82 Stinger and finally the current bold C5 model. Throughout the years, Corvette styling and performance have constantly been improved and refined until reaching its current status as an automotive icon. Four Decades of unprecedented success have established the Corvette as America's preeminent sports car. The 45th Anniversary set is a tribute to the impact and longevity of this fiberglass fantasy car.

Convertables:
[[File:Convertables.png|300px|right]] '''Convertables''' was a short-lived series of [[Hot Wheels]] cars produced in 1991. Their gimmick was their ability to change color and shape when the cars were put in hot or cold water when color shifted. Three segments of the Convertables lines were advertised; ''Wreckers'', ''Hot Rods'' and ''Roadsters'', of which the ''Roadsters'' segment never made it into production. Each had their own gimmick; the ''Wreckers''' roofs would cave in or their hoods pop up, the ''Hot Rods'' would have blown engines pop up and the ''Roadsters'' would have their canvas tops pop up. Cyber Racers:
[[File:CyberRacers.jpg|200px|thumb]]'''Cyber Racers''' was a series of vehicles released by Hot Wheels in 1998. Each car has an LCD screen in the bottom with 2 buttons and a reset button on the top of the car. There were 2 different games, "Race Car" and "Crash Car". Race Car had 2 games in the screen, and 2 modes using the in built sensors that require the car to be on a track, Race and Drag. Crash Car had 2 games in the screen, and 2 modes using the in built sensors that require the car to be on a track, Crash and ???. In both games the car is represented on the screen has the Pontiac Grand Prix.

Cool Things:
[[File:Cool Thing Slime.JPG|250px]]

==Description==
This series of miniature toys is from the [https://www.coolthings.sm/?lang=en Cool Things Toy Company]. Can be found in many retail stores in boxes of surprise blind goodie bags, usually for a cheap price. Hot Wheels is not the only brand that the [https://www.coolthings.sm/?lang=en Cool Things Toy Company] uses as it is licensed with different brands to produces similar toys, or as they reefer "Pocket Money Toys".

Each car is roughly the size of similar series like the [[Atomix]] or [[Planet Micro]]. Though note the series has two different kinds of cars; "Flick Cars", which are activated by a key, and "Pull-Back Cars" which race when they are pulled back. The "Flick Cars" are a slightly smaller scale than the "Pull-Back Cars"

With each surprise baggie, not only will it come with one of the two types of cars, but will come with either Slime, Putty, or sometimes miniature track pieces.

The Pull-Back Cars were also marketed separately as '''Drifting Turbo Cars'''. This series gave the Pull-Back Cars official names.

Double Shotz (series):
Not to be confused with the [[Mitsubishi Double Shotz]]

The '''Double Shotz''' series is a short-lived [[2006]] toy line of pneumatic powered vehicles. Similar to a Bottle Rocket, water is put into these vehicles, a pump pressurizes air inside, and then when released, the pressure thrust the vehicle into fast speeds or heights. They featured a timer on the base which could be set to release a second 'boost' of power, hence the name '''Double Shotz'''.

Father's Day:
2008 brought the intial release of the '''Father's Day K-Mart Exclusives''' in place of [[Kmart Collector's Day]]. Not only would '''Hot Wheels''' collectors find this extraordinary 5 car series a big hit, but also any person or child looking to give a great gift for '''Father's Day'''. The [[Dairy Delivery]] with metal base was highly sought after by collectors.

In 2009 the series returned with 5 more hot castings... including the [['57 Buick]] making its first debut outside of the [[Ultra Hots Series]].

For 2015 another series consisting of 4 more castings has come out and being sold at Kmart and Kroger.

Faster Than Ever:
[[File:2423bf.jpg|right|150px]] This is a list of Hot Wheels '''''Faster Than Ever'' vehicles released between 2005-2006 & 2009-2010. To the right is what the Faster Than Ever''' wheel looks like, or also known as the [[FTE]]. The '''Faster Than Ever''' wheel is more than just a wheel. Its copper color signifies that the axle on that particular vehicle is nickel-plated. This nickel-plating of the axle creates an extra smooth surface (causing less friction) therefore, making the car faster than its non-nickel-plated counterparts. [[FTE]] wheels were brought back in 2009 due to a strong collector demand. These vehicles are sought after by any Hot Wheels Collector that loves to race their vehicles. The series was last seen in 2012 and currently remains inactive. This is a truly unique opportunity for the [[Hot Wheels]] collector. We asked our chief designer, [[Larry Wood]], to create vehicles that epitomize the excitement surrounding weekend custom car shows - proudly loading your cherry rod onto a rig that is as customized as its cargo, and anticipating the envious stares from fellow showmen. Taking inspiration from his real custom classics, Larry designed a chopped and channeled, wood paneled 1950 2-door Buick wagon appropriately named 'Elwoody', and an equally awesome customized Ford cab-over tow truck as its transport.

Elwoody Custom Cars proves that after 28 years, Larry Wood can still be counted on for amazing automotive designs.

Ed 'Big Daddy' Roth 4-Car Set:
[[File:Ed 'Big Daddy' Roth 4-Car Set2.JPG|center|800px]]

Before Ed Roth was nicknamed 'Big Daddy', He was simply known as the 'Crazy Painter'. Indeed, the creator of the famed 'Rat Fink' character, Wild Child, and a clan of other cult-like crazies which were emblazoned on T-shirts always had an eye for the edge. 'Big Daddy' used the money from the sale of those famous shirts to finance the construction of some of the most famous, imaginatively designed custom show cars in history.

100% Hot Wheels is proud to present this cavalcade of custom classics from Ed Roth's celebrated 40 year career. Four highly detailed models of 'Big Daddy's' most admired vehicles, ranging from the mildest to the wildest.

Fast & Furious Premium Series:
[[File:F-F-logo_zps58f75ca2.jpg|200px|right]]The '''''Fast & Furious''''' Premium Series is a series of [[Hot Wheels]] vehicles replicating real-life cars from the ''Fast & Furious'' film franchise. Unlike the 'Basic' [[Fast & Furious Series|''Fast & Furious'' Series]], these vehicles have detailed tampos, metal bases and [[Real Riders]] wheels. The series was dropped for 2022, with ''Fast & Furious''-themed Premium releases being put under the [[Replica Entertainment]] banner, before returning for 2023 using essentially the same release scheme as the previous year (i.e. with no specific theming or series).

El Camino 40th Anniversary 2-Car Set:
To those of us who find beauty in the trucks, the [[Chevrolet El Camino]] is the Mona Lisa of pickups. Introduced in 1959, the El Camino was designed as a truck in a car wrapping. For a span of nearly 30 years, Chevy produced model after model of these smartly styled pickup trucks, each with car-like luxury. Though production ended in 1988, the handsome pickups continue to be highly sought-after prizes for discriminating truck and car collectors.

The [['59 Chevrolet El Camino |'59]] looked like a rocket taking off. It featured bold front fenders that flowed back to sculpted gullwing fins. Its slender roof supports provided a nearly unobstructed view for maximum visibility as the scenery flew by.

Described as a "personal pickup", the [[1970 Chevy El Camino |1979 body style]] is most often voted "best-looking". It was built on the Chevelle platform and was beefed up to muscle car status with a 450 horsepower engine. The Super Sport accentuated with wide, bold racing stripes, was often seen "haulin" in the fast lane.

Fast & Furious Collector Set:
The second in a series of [[Premium Collector Set]]s was the Fast & Furious themed set. It featured three replicas and one truck which was not an exact replica of any vehicle seen in The Fast and The Furious films, but was inspired by 'The Racers Edge' deco on the [[Ford F-150 SVT Lightning]] driven by Brian O'Conner (Paul Walker).

The [[Volkswagen Jetta MK3]] is identical to the one used in the [[Fast_&_Furious_Premium_Series#Original_Fast|Fast & Furious Premium Series]]. The [[Toyota Supra]] and [['70 Dodge Charger R/T]] are positioned like the iconic drag race at the end of The Fast and The Furious (2001) and even includes a clear plastic stand to prop the Dodge Charger into a wheelstand position.

Extreme Shoxx:
[[File:ExtremeShoxx.png|200px|right]]'''Extreme Shoxx''' was a short-lived series of Hot Wheels cars produced from 2014 to 2015 as part of Hot Wheels's "Off Road" segments. The selling point of the cars was their "Extreme Shoxx suspension", which featured a screw-like system which would adjust tension on a flexible plastic spring to give the cars more or less suspension depending on how the system was adjusted; this would adjust two adjusting pivoting points on the main chassis. The series did not continue beyond 2015, likely due to poor sales. 2015 releases excluding the yellow Da'Kar were not widely distributed and some unknown releases may exist. Farbs:
[[File:FARBs.png|300px|right]][[File:35 Years of Speed Randy Leffingwell Farbs (6).JPG|300px|right]]'''Farbs''' (also formatted as '''FARBs''') was a very short-lived series of tongue-in-cheek vehicles produced in 1972. Advertised as "Fantastic Car Kooks", these were a series of cartoonish "people" cars, with people acting as the bodies and wheels attached to their arms and legs. The series was the brainchild of independent toy designer [[wikipedia:Eddy Goldfarb|Eddy Goldfarb]]; the series was named after Goldfarb as tribute. While the series was manufactured by Mattel and feature wheels also used on Hot Wheels products these were not officially branded as Hot Wheels products. Only a single series of four cars were produced; two more, named [[Bye-A-Nose]] and [[Wyndan Cheeks]], were slated to be produced but never got past prototyping. Electric Hot Wheels Racing:
{{Stub}} [[File:Its Electric bogey wogey.jpg|300px|right]] The''' Electric Hot Wheels Racing''' or '''Electric Hot Wheels''' series is a series of Hot Wheel Slot cars that came out mostly in the late 1990s, with some appearances afterwards mostly in tracksets. Slot cars are miniature cars that have motors in them which are powered by a rail system. When the rail is electrified, the electricity is transferred through the slot car's connectors and into the motor, making the car move on track. Giving a slot car more electricity gives the car more speed, but too much speed might make the car wipe out on any turn. So using the controller, you must increase and decrease the speed of the slot car in order to beat your opponents. Slot car sets first came out in the 1910s, only having a "boom" in the 1960s early 70's, and then in the 1990, with partnership of Tyco, Hot Wheels made their own 1:87-1:60 scale slot cars. FAO Schwarz Hot Wheels Factory:
The '''Hot Wheels Factory Experience''' opened at the [[FAO Schwarz]] location in New York. The experience consisted of a kiosk where the customer would go through four steps, choosing the model, choosing the color, choosing the engine, and finally choosing the tires. After the customer chose their options, a short 3d animation of the vehicle being assembled would play, and the physical car would come through a shoot to the customer along with a certificate. The only options that would change the physical vehicle are the model and color choice. Every vehicle available was a premium casting with an acrylic case. The experience opened in 2004 and continued until at least 2007. At opening, it only included the [[Ford Mustang GT Concept (100%)|Ford Mustang GT Concept]], [[Corvette C6 Convertible (100%)|Corvette C6]], [[Hummer H2 (2004)|Hummer H2]], and [[1971 Camaro]]. In 2005, the [[Enzo Ferrari (100%)|Enzo Ferrari]] and [[Dodge Viper GTS]] were also made available.

Fright Cars Series:
'''Fright Cars''' were originally a series of '''Wal-Mart''' Exclusive Cars on single cards, in 2006. In 2007 '''Target''' had their own Exclusive '''5 Pack''' set to add to the series, also known as the [[Fright Cars 5-Pack]] / [[Gift Pack]] set, and the [[Target]] Exclusive [[Gift Pack]] was called Scary Cars 5-Pack in 2008. Even before 2006 '''Mattel''' had a series called [[Halloween Highway Series]] that ran from 2002 to 2004, that were 4 different 2 car packs. After 2005 the team at [[Hot Wheels]] saw the demand of bringing back the series to the Hot Wheels collector again in 2006. In 2008, as part of a [[Wal-Mart]] Exclusive, '''Hot Wheels''' added a twist for the collector again, by adding the [[Chase]] Car into the Fright Car Series only on a single card 8 car set. The [[Chase]] Car for 2008 is called '''Invisible''' [[Phastasm]], it makes it's second debut in this series. The first was in 2006 Fright Cars Series, and this time around it makes a great come back for the [[Chase]] Car. The '''Invisible Phastasm''' is an all clear plastic car, just leaving the rim of the [[OH5]] Chrome and the axles to only have Metal. Although there wasn't a Halloween assortment in 2018, [[The Nightmare Before Christmas 25 Years Series|"The Nightmare Before Christmas" 25 Years set]] was released in autumn as a Kroger store exclusive and might be considered a substitute assortment for the frightful season. ==[[Fright Cars Series (2006)|2006 Fright Cars Series]]== Single cards {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size: 90%; text-align: left" width="100%" ! Final Run Series:
[[Image:Final Run Logo.JPG|center|500px]] '''Final Run''' was an annual commemorative series released by Hot Wheels as part of their annual assortments from [[1999]] to [[2005]], with the exception of [[2000]]. The series featured a number of models which were slated to be retired by Mattel, never to be released again. As part of Mattel's vow to never release these castings again, their tools were cut in half and destroyed as a result, with these last releases receiving special paintjobs and logos commemorating their retirement from the series. Earlier iterations of castings featured in this series were given special wheels, either Real Riders or Pro Circuit multi-piece wheels, but this was dropped in 2003. A number of highly popular castings ended up in this series. [[:Category:Final Run Series|Category Final Run Series]] ==1999== The castings in the series this year were packaged in an exterior ornamental sleeve packaging. The sleeves featured circular tape on the side reading "Not Returnable If Opened"; the cards themselves are held in a cardboard backing with cutouts for the J-hook. The back of each ornamental sleeve packaging had a few factoids about each retiring casting. Fuel Altereds Vintage Drag 2-Car Set:
[[File:2001_Fuel_Altereds_Vintage_Drags.JPG|500px]]

The Fuel Altered class has facetiously been called "drag racing's most exciting 3/8ths of a mile" because the ultra powerful cars were impossible to steer in a straight line, thus causing them to travel more than 1/4 mile before hitting the finish line.

Ironically, the fuel was not altered - it was the wheelbase. Owners would shorten the wheel bases and drop in huge engines.. the lightweight car bodies were often afterthoughts. These radical and frequently uncontrollable rods were crowd favorites during the '50s and '60s and went on to become among the most popular cars in drag racing history.

100% Hot Wheels has recreated two legendary cars from the cherished era. Pure Hell and Winged express are so hot they might make your eyes burn just by looking at them. And they are sure to create great memories for those who loved drag racing's Fuel Altered class.

Foose Design 2-Car Set:
[[File:FooseDesignBoxFront.JPG|500px]]

In the world of custom automobiles, some may consider [[wikipedia:Chip Foose|Chip Foose]] to be a new kid on the block, but in reality he possesses a rich background in the custom car culture. Not only is his father a well-known car designer, but also Chip has worked and honed his craft in the elite of customizing shops. During his apprenticeship, Chip talents grew and matured to equal and/or surpass that of his mentors.

As tangible proof, we offer two of Chip's finest creations as the Foose Design vehicle set. HemisFear and Manhattan are two sleek and elegant vehicles each incorporating design elements from '30's classics as well as cutting-edge futuristic concepts. These beautiful cars firmly establish Chips reputation as a custom-car builder who is successful by design.

Gone in Sixty Seconds 4-Car Set:
Gone In 60 Seconds, which refers to the length of time it takes a professional thief to make your car... his car, is a remake of the 1974 cult classic, made famous by its spectacular 40 minute police chase during which 93 cars were destroyed. 

The updated story finds legendary car thief and auto aficionado, Randall "Memphis" Raines, being forced back into a life of crime to save the life of his kid brother, who has become entangled in a dangerous high-stakes caper. With more star power and horsepower than Hollywood has seen in years, this fast-paced action thriller promises to blow the covers off the valves at the summer box office.

To commemorate the Jerry Bruckheimer production of Gone In 60 Seconds, HOT WHEELS COLLECTIBLES' has replicated four hot cars from the film, including a classic '49 Merc, a striking Dodge Viper GTS, a custom '67 Mustang and a cab-over truck! Don't wait to get your hands on this highly collectible car set , because it too could be gone in 60 seconds.

'''General Mill's Salute to Richard Petty''' was a set of 18 vehicles produced in 2004. All vehicles (with the exception of the [[Volkswagen Drag Bus]]) had opaque black windows with no interior.

==Project Green Flag==
In a October - December 2019 Newsletter article, Hot Wheels & General Mills worked on a project internally dubbed "Project Green Flag" which ended up becoming the General Mills promotion for the "Salute to Richard Petty" series. The article goes into details about how tricky it was to to ship loose Hot Wheels into cereal boxes, and the creation of the drop baggies that the cars where into to protect them from the cereal, and vise versa, protect the cereal from paint contamination.

The article shows off Prototypes as well. Most notably indicating that in the early stages, [[Purple Passion]] & the [['65 Chevy Impala]] where to be apart of the series, but ended up being dropped.

Funny Car Summer 2-Car Set:
[[Image:Funny Car Summer 2-Car Set.JPG|center|600px]]

It was the summer of '72 and a new class of racing called Funny Car was growing in popularity across the nation. The top places to race were the drag strips of Southern California where innovators were pulling up awesome times. Big John Mazmanian was running a Plymouth Barracuda that was smokin' the competition when Nelson Carter arrived from Oklahoma. Having established track records all across the country with his "Super Chief" Dodge Charger, the charismatic Carter became Big John's main competition and set the stage for a series of legendary match races. Their heated, yet friendly, rivalry is one reason the dog days of '72 became known as the Funny Car Summer!

Ferrari X-V:
[[File:Ferrari XV Logo.png|right|175px]]
[[File:Ferrari XV Asset.png|right|175px]]
'''Ferrari X-V''' was a short-lived series of [[Hot Wheels]] cars that was released in [[2005]] only. This was an offshoot of the [[Motorized X-V Racers]] series. As with the normal series, the cars are charged by a Power Base Booster, but in this series it was known as the X-V Power Booster. The X-V Power Booster is significantly larger than the standard Power Base Booster and is only compatible with cars from the series. The series attempted to celebrate Ferrari design by merging Ferrari design with futuristic concepts. The "X-V" in this case stood for "'''X'''treme '''V'''elociti".

Flippers:
[[Image:FlippersLogo.png|center|300px]] ==Description== '''Flippers''' (later '''Flashmagic Flippers''', conceptualized as '''Flipside Wheels''') was a series that debuted in [[1990]]. All castings were designed by [[Lionel]], originally released as "Lionel Revolvers" in years prior. All models were made and manufactured by Chief Industrial Co. out of China. The series was pitched to [[Hot Wheels]] rather than a formal collaboration using a hand-drawn pitch board and mock-up prototype. Mattel omitted licensed insignias from all tampo graphics before release under Hot Wheels branding. In [[1991]] Mattel retooled a single model to include lights and sounds with a non-rechargeable battery for three releases and changed the name of the series to Flashmagic Flippers. Formula Fuelers:
[[File:FormulaFuelers.gif|right|200x200px]] [[File:Formula Fuelers Promo.jpg|right|200x200px]] '''Formula Fuelers''' was a short-lived series of oversized battery-operated Hot Wheels cars and motorcycles which ran from 2004 to 2005. The Formula Fuelers were unique in that these cars were "powered" by what Hot Wheels called "Nitrox2" fitted in canisters which would be plugged into the cars; the idea here was that kids could mix whatever liquids they had from orange juice to coke and place them in the canister to see how far the car would go. Each car came with a number of Nitrox2-branded packets, filled with "tablets" and "liquid". When the canister was plugged in, a button on the vehicle could be pressed and the vehicle would go; the cars were advertised as being able to go faster "the better you mix", encouraging kids to experiment. The cars and motorcycles are approximately 1/24 scale, with the 2004 Racers and the 2005 Sky Force, bar the Motos, having sound effects and playing them as the vehicle moved along. In actuality, the Nitrox2 was essentially just effervescent sodium tablets which were "activated" by the Nitrox2-branded liquid, likely colored water; on the packaging of most Formula Fuelers products, these warned the buyer that the Nitrox2 tablets should only be used with liquids such as water, fruit juices or soda. The canisters, when plugged in, didn't actually fuel the cars in a normal sense; each canister had two electrical contacts which when plugged in completed the internal electrical circuits and allowed the cars to run, with electricity flowing through the liquid in the canister. The sodium content in the liquid determined how far the vehicles went; the more sodium was present, the farther the vehicle would run. The vehicles were all powered by 3 "AA" batteries. The series may have been quite popular during its time; the series also spawned a Flash video game on the Hot Wheels website titled ''Formula Fuelers Racers''. Frankford Candy Container Cars:
'''Frankford Candy Container Cars''' were a set of large scale all plastic cars filled with candy distributed by the Frankford Candy & Chocolate company for the US, they were produced in Mexico by ''Bondy Fiesta''. They did not come in packaging, only having plastic wrapped around the car with a barcode and nutrition facts, sold to stores in a 12 count box branded as ''Car Dispenser with Candy Cars inside''.  Some have a base with ©2004 and a ''Bondy Fiesta'' logo and others have a China ©2005 base with a larger door for candy with no ''Bondy Fiesta'' logo.  They all used pre-existing mainline designs, including: [[Vulture]], [[Sinistra]], [[Sling Shot]], [[Side Draft]], [[Pony Up]], and [[40 Somethin']]. ''Bondy Fiesta'' continued to release these castings in Mexico after 2005, for those versions see [[Bondy Fiesta Candy Container Cars]]. Note: This list is not complete, many color variants exist.

Flamethrowers:
[[File:Flamethrowers.png|200px|right]]

Released: 2003

Status: Discontinued

Flamethrowers,  also known as Supercharged Flamethrowers, are an assortment of motorized light and sound vehicles released in 2003. As part of a new light and sound vehicle lineup, these cars feature flame-shooting exhaust pipes with flames that pop out and light up when the rear spoiler is pressed down. When the button on the roof is pressed, the car will race off and will reveal a hidden "Nitrox 2 Fuel cell". The light up flames inside the exhaust pipes will flash, and the exposed engine will also shake. There were 3 different versions of vehicles in the Flamethrowers assortment, all with different color schemes. the Tuner, Hatchback, and the Supercar, which was released in the later half of 2003. The Supercar version can also talk.

Formula One Collection:
[[File:F1Collection.png|200px|right]]'''Formula One Collection''' is a [[Hot Wheels Premium|Premium]] series of Hot Wheels vehicles depicting Formula One cars. This series was introduced in collaboration with Formula One Management. Each vehicle comes packaged with a simple plastic display stand featuring the team's name, with the car screwed onto the plastic base.

A pre-sale for the first three waves of vehicles was released through [[Mattel Creations]] and replicates the cars used in the [[wikipedia:2024 Formula One World Championship|2024 Formula One World Championship]]; the vehicles themselves are available at retail stores.
