[[File:HotWheelsHighway35WorldRace.png.png|center|300px]] ==Description== ''Please check out the other [[Highway 35 World Race (disambiguation)|World Race]] pages listed by relevancy'' The '''World Race''' series debuted in [[2003]] under the [[Highway 35]] anniversary label, released to coincide with the [[Hot Wheels: World Race (film)|''Hot Wheels: World Race'']] film of the same name. Models of this series were distributed and commonly available across the United States, Canada, Europe, and certain Latin American regions. It consisted of five subsets (Wave Rippers, Street Breed, Road Beasts, Dune Ratz, Scorchers) of seven models each. According to [[Eric Tscherne]] five new models ([[Switchback]], [[24/Seven]], [[Zotic]], [[Wild Thing]], [[1/4 Mile Coupe]]) were created for each team of this series; all debuted in the [[Mainline]] prior. Blister pack also contained a collectible token and numbered comic book. Gran Toros:
[[File:GranToros.png|300px|right]]
'''Gran Toros''' is an early line of 1/43 scale Hot Wheels manufactured by [[Mebetoys]] for Mattel from 1970 to 1973. The line was created by Mattel after acquiring Mebetoys and introduced to the American market in 1970 as a larger scale version of the standard Hot Wheels lineup; the line was given the name of '''Sputafuoco''' (lit. "fire-breathing") and '''Heisse Räder Supergroß''' (lit. "Hot Wheels Super Big") in Italy and Germany respectively.

Each of the models feature intricately designed parts and movable parts. All castings were made in Italy by Mebetoys; many of the models in this series were created by Mebetoys specifically for this line, while others were modified from older Mebetoys models. After the discontinuation of the line, some Gran Toros models were modified for use in the Mebetoys line, usually through the addition of disc-style plastic wheels for cost-cutting.

Heavyweights:
[[File:1972 Toys & Hobbies catalog Heavyweights.jpg|right|400px]]
The Heavyweights were a series of futuristic trucks in 1970 and 1971 designed predominately by Ira Gilford and sometimes with the help of Larry Wood. They used three different bodies with a plastic attachment on the back. Once the plastic attachment is missing, they are indistinguishable from each other. Most of the plastic attachments, glass and interiors have been reproduced.

High Speed Racing Wheels Series:
This is a list of all vehicles from the '''High Speed Racing Wheels Series'''. Under assortment BDW18, produced in 2014. It was a continuation of the [[Team Hot Wheels High-Speed Wheel Series|Team Hot Wheels High-Speed Wheel Series]]. All cars featured the [[HSRW]] Wheel which was unique to this series. Graphics were directed by [[Jeremy Cox]]Hot Wheels Showcase App Vehicles from this series are hard to find. Of the 25 vehicles planned, only 18 are known to have been released. Original distribution of the series was limited to specific retailers (such as Kohl's) in each region which contributed to their limited availability. Cars #1-11 appear to have been released in the United States. Gran Turismo Series:
[[File:Gran Turismo logo.jpg|250px]]

Gran Turismo is a video game series developed by Polyphony Digital for the Playstation console. It is a racing style game known for its large selection of vehicles. Since debuting in 1997, the series has sold over 77 million copies making it the highest-selling franchise for Playstation.
Hot Wheels has made several series in conjunction with the game.

==2016 Gran Turismo Series==
[[File:03012.jpg|thumb|left|500px]]
The '''Gran Turismo Series''' features 8 different models that first showed up in Europe retail stores in April 2016. In the United States the series was a "Hobby Exclusive", meaning none of the big box retail stores were able to order them. The first US-based cases appeared in late May 2016. Some of the models first appeared in Gran Turismo 5 while the rest appeared in its successor, Gran Turismo 6. The Jaguar XJ220, first appeared in its racing-modified form in the original PlayStation-exclusive Gran Turismo 2.

Hemmings Motor News 2-Vehicle Set:
[[Image:Hemmings Motor News 2-Car Set.JPG|center|500px]] Hemmings Motor News is a monthly magazine considered by many to be "the Bible" for vintage car enthusiasts. Between its sepia-toned covers are thousands of old cars, trucks and other vehicles for sale as well as invaluable information on parts, services, and high performance packages. No matter what state you or your car happen to be in, Hemmings Motor News offers quick and easy ways to add a special touch of class to your classic. Hot Wheels Classics:
[[File:Hwclassics.jpg|200px|right]]
'''Hot Wheels Classics''' is an annual line of [[Hot Wheels]] cars first released in 2005. They are marketed towards adult collectors and were originally priced around $3.99 ([[Wikipedia:United States Dollar|USD]]). Each car features a metal base and is released in several different [[Spectraflame]] colors. Series 1 was released in 2005, series 2 in 2006, series 3 in 2007, series 4 in 2008, and series 5 in 2009.

In 2008 First to the Market was the Vintage Classics with [[Collector's Button]] in celebration of 40 years of [[Hot Wheels]].

Holiday Hot Rods:
Holiday Hot Rods are a series of Exclusive Cars, in Celebration for the Holiday Seasons that started in 2006 that were sold Exclusively at [[Wal-Mart]] on single cards, below are the following years, starting with 2006. Then in 2007, [[Target]] joined in with their series the 3 pack Holiday Hot Rods as both retail stores carried the brands into 2009. Not to be confused with the [[Holiday Rods]], as they were issued by [[Mattel]] and any vendor through Mattel can sell these to distribute to their patrons, or [[Holiday Racers Series]] began in 2017. Starting in [[2020]], the line, though similarly themed, was renamed to "[[Winter Series]]" ==2006== ===[[Holiday Hotrods Series (2006)|2006 Holiday Hot Rods]]===

== Description==
In the 1950s and the car is king. On warm summer nights, girls wearing poodle skirts and guys sporting varsity jackets cruise Main Street in their hot cars. They pull up at their favorite hangout - the drive-in restaurant - where car hops on rollerskates bring trays loaded with hamburgers, french fries and milkshakes right to the cars. Radios blare the hottest rock 'n' roll music. Boys rev their engines and girls whisper and giggle. Here's a piece of yesterday that we've created just for you.

==='57 Chevy===
The 1957 Chevy with a 350 cubic inch V8 engine was the muscle car of the decade. Edging out the competition with real horsepower and performance, it embodied the need for speed and power!

===Purple Passion ===
This custom bad boy was everyone's favorite. The chopped and channeled 1951 Mercury owned the road with an overpowering chrome front-end grille that let everyone know it was there!

===1959 Cadilliac Eldorado===
In an era where tail fins defined style, the 1959 Eldorado was the biggest shark on the road. With a 300 cid V8 engine producing 345 hp, you had it made in the shade!

===1959 Impala Lowrider===
It was all about style and beauty - and being the lowest car on the boulevard. This customized 1959 Impala Lowrider with classic gullwing rear fender design and "cat's eyes" taillights had it all!

Holiday Rods:
'''Holiday Rods''' are a series of cars in celebration of the holiday season. They were released between [[List of 2004 Hot Wheels|2004]] - [[List of 2009 Hot Wheels|2009]]. Unlike the [[Holiday Hot Rods]],''' Holiday Rods''' were not exclusive to any store. [[Holiday Racers Series|Holiday Racers mainline segment]] began in [[List of 2017 Hot Wheels|2017]]. == 2004== The following castings were released in the 2004 '''Holiday Rods''' series:

Hot Wheels Haulers:
'''Haulers''' was a series of trucks released from 1997 to 2002. This series was produced by ARCO Toys until at least 2000 when any mention of ARCO Toys was dropped from packaging. Some castings were also used in playsets and [[Super Race Rigs]] packs. Packaging for this series never featured casting names.

Hot Wheels 30th Anniversary:
[[File:30th Ann Poster.JPG|300px|right]] To celebrate 30 years of Hot Wheels, Mattel released 30 models. one for each year. Next to those 30 models, a boxed set of those same 30 models was released. All models came in their period appropriate package and in a blue box. Additionally Hot Wheels chose the first original in-house designed concept vehicle the TWIN MILL as a "flagship" to commemorate the series.
These Collector's Edition Vehicles were created exclusively for the 30th Anniversary of Hot Wheels. Hot & Classic - Bugs & Buses 4-Car Set:
"Shortly after Ferdinand Porsche first introduced Germany's 'Peoples Car' more than five decades ago, Volkswagen's Beetle and Microbus became automotive phenomena. The cute, durable, rear-engine vehicles were so popular during the '60's, 70's, and '80's that it was almost impossible to find a street or stretch of road in America that didn't have at least two or three cruisin' along. Their pleasing lines are so classic in style that they have become popular vehicles within the custom car culture. Accordingly, 100% Hot Wheels proudly offers the Hot & Classic Bugs & Buses set. Each model is offered as a showroom beauty and as a cool customized cruiser."

Hot Wheels Monster Trucks:
[[File:HWMT.png|frameless|475px]]
'''Hot Wheels Monster Trucks''' is a monster truck series introduced by [[Mattel]] in 2018 as the successor to Mattel's long-running [[Monster Jam]] toy line. The series features original Hot Wheels designs, monster truck versions of classic Hot Wheels vehicles, licensed vehicles, and trucks featured in [[#Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live|Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live]].
==Releases by Year== {{HWMT|header=no}} ==About the Series== Following its introduction in 2018, '''Hot Wheels Monster Trucks''' expanded into numerous themed collections, multipacks, playsets and related product lines. The brand also expanded into live entertainment with [[#Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live|Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live]]. Since its introduction in 2018, the brand has expanded beyond the main 1:64 scale line to include larger-scale vehicles, multipacks, playsets, themed series and several related Monster Trucks product lines. ==Notes== * Monster Trucks releases in 2019, 2022, 2023 and 2024 included Connect and Crash Cars as bonus vehicles. * Monster Trucks releases in 2020 included Crushable Cars as bonus vehicles. * Monster Trucks releases in 2021 included Re-Crushable Cars as bonus vehicles. ==Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live== [[File:0B517BE2-478C-478A-930D-5655C3FBDDED.png|right|250px]] '''Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live''' is a live touring monster truck show based on the Hot Wheels Monster Trucks brand. The tour was announced in November 2018 and held its first events in January 2019, bringing full-size versions of Hot Wheels Monster Trucks such as [[Bone Shaker (Monster Truck)|Bone Shaker]] and Tiger Shark to arenas alongside [[Bigfoot]]. The tour has since expanded internationally, bringing Hot Wheels Monster Trucks to life through jumps, stunts, crashing and smashing in live arena performances. ==Bonus vehicles== ===Connect and Crash Cars=== In all 2019 releases of the Monster Trucks, they came with a Connect and Crash Car. These cars resemble Hot Wheels castings released in previous years ([[Time Attaxi]], [[Rally Cat]], [[Dawgzilla]] and [[Cruise Bruiser]]) and were designed by [[Brendon Vetuskey]]. They were released in red, orange, yellow, green and blue, with colors selected by [[Jeremy Cox]]. These cars can be attached to and stacked on each other. Connect and Crash Cars returned in 2022 and were used again in the 2023 and 2024 lines. ===Crushable Cars=== In 2020 Connect and Crash Cars were replaced by a Crushable Cars. Like Connect and Crash Cars these cars were released in red, orange, yellow, green and blue. These however are completely fictional cars and do not resemble any released car to date. These were designed by [[Brendon Vetuskey]] and the colors selected by [[Jeremy Cox]]. ===Crashed Die-Cast Cars=== In 2020 brand new Crashed Die-Cast Cars come as a bonus cars to a special wave of Hot Wheels Monster Trucks. These bonus cars were designed by [[Brendon Vetuskey|Brendon Vetuskey.]] He utilized existing Hot Wheels castings as a starting point, modifying every distinguishing detail to take it from licensed to unlicensed, then proceeded to crush the cars in the digital world, ultimately creating four brand-new designs. [[File:HotTunerzlogo.png|200px|right]] '''Hot Tunerz''' (also called "Car Tunerz") are vehicles inspired by the tuner scene of 2000s, in a cartoonish theme. They are similar to the [['Tooned]] series of cars, some castings were reused for that series. They were released in both 1:55 scale and 1:20 scale. This series was designed by [[Eric Tscherne]]. Hot Wheels Boulevard:
[[File:Boulevard2020.png|right|200px]]'''Hot Wheels Boulevard''' is an adult collector-focused [[Hot Wheels Premium|premium series]] consisting of a wide range of vehicles with [[Real Riders]] wheels, diecast bodies and chassis; it acted as a successor to [[Hot Wheels Garage (2011)|Hot Wheels Garage]]. Originally introduced in [[2012 Hot Wheels Boulevard|2012]] with vehicles themed to a certain theme, the series was rebooted in [[2020 Hot Wheels Boulevard|2020]] with more realistically-styled vehicles, described by Mattel as having "Premium execution and awesome decos that command attention in any collection". The rebooted series is a Walmart exclusive in the United States.

Hot Wheels RC:
[[File:HotWheelsRC.png|center|500x500px]] ==Description== Released originally as an [[Red Line Club]] exclusive with the [[Cybertruck]], it then was released to the public in 2020. Originally, each set come with a 1/64 version of a special car, the remote to go with it, and a Hot Wheels Track piece to insert into any track so that your remote control vehicle can easily get onto a Hot Wheels track to perform more stunts. However, starting with the 2025 Ford Mustang GTD at the very least, the Hot Wheels Track piece has been eliminated. The cars themselves are heavily modified to have the remote control mechanics inside them. Other than that they look nearly identical to their normal basic line versions, apart from the totally plastic construction. Just an additional thrill to anyone who enjoys classic Hot Wheels castings. Hot Wheels Crayons:
'''Hot Wheels Longer Lasting Crayons''' were a series of crayons in the shape of Hot Wheels cars which were manufactured in 1989 by the Craft House Corporation (Toledo, Ohio) under license by Mattel. There were 8 different Hot Wheels castings represented in crayon form. They were commonly packaged in packets of four crayons (sometimes packages of five) of which two different assortment of castings could be found. Each car could be found in eight different colors.

Hot Shots:
[[File:HotShots.png|right|200px]]'''Hot Shots''' was an extremely short-lived series of motorized cars and dragsters produced during the [[Redline]] era from [[1972]] to [[1973]]. The selling point of the castings was their use of RipFire motors, which were essentially extremely powerful ripcord motors allowing for the castings to wheelie and burnout. The cars, advertised as "Power racers with ''RipFire'' motors", were also purportedly able to spark as they burned out. While the series was manufactured by Mattel and feature wheels also used on Hot Wheels products these were not officially branded as Hot Wheels products.

The original two dragster castings have also been known to have been made in Mexico. Hot Shots castings are now noted to be extremely expensive to acquire today.

Hot Wheels 30th Anniversary 4-Car Set:
[[Image:Hot Wheels 30th Anniversary Set.JPG|center|800px]] Released in 1998 celebrating our 30th anniversary, we have issued collector - quality recreations of four awesome cars from our popular 1970 Spoiler series. Spoilers were maxed-out muscle cars that looked like no other 1:64 scale diecast vehicles at that time. These promotional cars featured huge supercharged engines, sparkling mag wheels, [[RL|Red Line tires]], cool colors and of course, "spoilers" for peak performance. In 1970, the [[Heavy Chevy]], [[King 'Kuda]], [[Light My Firebird]], and [[Nitty Gritty Kitty]] hit the tracks with major attitudes... attitudes that have lasted for 3 decades. All vehicles had graphics done by [[David McDonald]] and made in China. Hot Wheels Apptivity:
[[File:Apptivity™ Hot Wheels™ TV Commercial|500px|center]]

From Mattel's gaming app service "Apptivity" (pronounced App-tivity), a line of Hot Wheels was produced for the game. These 1/64 castings had several buttons on the bottom called "Retractable Touch Points" that were used to control the in-game car with the physical diecast. As the name insinuates, pressing the center white button on the bottom retracts the touch points inside the body of the car itself, allowing for use of these cars on track layouts. The app, called Mattel Apptivity, was available for free only on the Apple App Store until it was cancelled in late 2013-early 2014. Contrary to popular belief, these castings had no electronic components.

All castings from this line were exclusive, and some featured [[Team Hot Wheels]] themed liveries.

This line was available in ''Apple'' stores and select other retailers, and the Mattel Apptivity app itself was only available for iPad devices on the ''Apple App Store''.

For more info, check [https://m.service.mattel.com/us/Technical/productDetail?prodno=Y2409&siteid=27 here].

Hot Import Nights:
The Hot Import Nights (HIN) and HIN D-Force series were two series of 1:50 scale cars produced by Hot Wheels in 2004 in cooperation with the car show company Hot Import Nights. Each series consisted of four castings, and each casting was released in three colors. "Hot Import Nights produces awesome automotive events featuring the hottest music, models, and cars, and providing the ultimate entertainment from the cutting edge of the car culture - Tuners and Drifters." Hot Line:
[[File:HotLine.png|300px|right]]'''Hot Line''' was a very short-lived series of motorized model trains using [[Sizzlers]] technology. These were produced in 1971 and were approximately 1/64 scale. The trains were able to run on Sizzlers-style track known as Railtrack and consisted of a futuristic high-speed train with some outlandish elements and a number of other cars to go alongside it. The trains were able to stop and go using buttons and were recharged using the Sizzlers [[Juice Machine (Sizzlers)|Juice Machine]] or [[Power Pit]] with a special adapter. Despite sharing a similar name and using Hot Wheels-style technology this series was not officially branded as a Hot Wheels product although they were considered a Hot Wheels product in some material. [[Hot Wheels Railroad]] can be seen as sort of a spiritual successor to this series.

Hot Wheels Premium:
[[File:PremiumGoldLabel.png|right|200px]]'''Hot Wheels Premium''' is the adult-focused sub-segment of the Hot Wheels lineup; it is the middle rung of the main four Hot Wheels lines of vehicles, slotted above the [[mainline]] and [[themed assortment]]s but below the [[Red Line Club|Red Line Club exclusives]]. Typically, Premium vehicles have metal bodies and bases, rubber wheels and more detailed tampos than their mainline counterparts. Although Premium series have existed for some time, the logo and name for this segment of Hot Wheels was adopted in 2019. The Premium line adopted a gold-colored logo in 2024 although the basic design of the logo remained unchanged; this logo is colloquially known as the "gold label".

Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Oversized:
[[File:Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Oversized logo.jpg|right|200px]]'''Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Oversized''' is a sub series of [[Hot Wheels Monster Trucks]] first launched in [[2018]]. This line features 1/24 scale versions of various Monster Truck models; they feature a special package design which can be used as a display case. The series gained its current name in 2021; prior to then, the series was simply known as '''Monster Trucks 1:24 Scale Trucks'''. Some trucks in this line have not been released in 1/64 scale form.

Hot Wheels RacerVerse:
[[File:RacerVerse.png|200px|right]]'''Hot Wheels RacerVerse''' was a series of 1/64 scale cartoonish-style Hot Wheels cars running from [[2023]] to [[2026]]; it acted as the effective replacement for [[Character Cars]]. These cars put characters from various film properties into stylized vehicles taking after their personality. This series was handled by [[Kevin Cao]], [[Mike Vasquez]] and [[Rich Orlina]]. All vehicles were made in Thailand. This series was discontinued in [[2026]] and replaced by [[Superstar Speeders]].

Hot Wheels (comics):
[[Image:HW Comics.JPG|right|200px|thumb|All Six HW Comic Books]] In 1970, [[DC Comics]] released the comic series,'''Hot Wheels''' which revolved around the main character [[Jack Wheeler]] & friends as they race and save the day in Hot Wheel cars. Only 6 issues where ever publish. A [[Hot Wheels (TV series)|TV series]] was released alongside the comics. ==Comics== *[[Hot Wheels Issue 1]]
NO.1 APR. (March April 1970) *[[Hot Wheels Issue 2]]
NO.2 JUNE (May June 1970] *[[Hot Wheels Issue 3]]
NO.3 AUG. (July August 1970) *[[Hot Wheels Issue 4]]

NO.5 DEC. (Nov Dec 1970) *[[Hot Wheels Issue 6]]
NO.6 FEB. [ Jan Feb 1971) ==Fun Fact== The Hot Wheels "Universe" seems to revolve around the Wheeler family. Over 30 years later, [[Jack Wheeler]] is portrayed as a father to his son Vert Wheeler in the [[Highway 35 World Race]]. Hot Wheels Customs:
'''Hot Wheels Customs''' was an online-exclusive Hot Wheels line that let customers produce a personalized Hot Wheels car that ran from 2011-2012. There were five available castings to choose from with existing tampos. At launch, the [[Dairy Delivery]] and [[Purple Passion]] were available to choose from. While in the Spring of 2011, the [[Hiway Hauler (1992)|Hiway Hauler]], [[School Busted]], and [[Surfin' School Bus]] becomes available for purchase. After customers choose one of the five castings, they can upload an image for the casting. In the next step, customers can choose a frame for the image and position it within the frame. Then they can add a message up to 18 characters long. Finally, they can choose various packaging options for their vehicle, such as a “Happy Birthday” message. The cars were priced at $7.99 each plus shipping and packaging, and there is an order quantity limit of 50 per car all customers can create. After the line was discontinued in December 2012, four of the models without tampos were available for purchase on the [[HotWheelsCollectors.com]] website under the series "HW Designs". Hot Wheels: Extreme Racing:
[[Image:Extremeracing.jpg|thumb|300px]]
'''Hot Wheels: Extreme Racing''' is a Playstation Video Game published by THQ in 2001.

In this game, players race [[Hot Wheels]] vehicles on the road, on the sea and in the air. The player begins with Three vehicles, and is able to unlock and upgrade more during the game.

The game includes multi-player modes for up to four people.

{{Game tep|title1=Hot Wheels: Ultimate Racing.|image1=Hot Wheels Ultimate Racing.jpg|caption1=The Game Cover.|developers=Raylight Studios|publishers=DSI Games|platforms=PlayStation Portable.|releases=NA: June 19th 2007

'''''Hot Wheels: Ultimate Racing''''' is a game developed by Italian company Raylight Studios and published by DSI Games for the PlayStation Portable (PSP) released  on June 19th [[2007]], Hot Wheels Ultimate Racing is a game with over 26 cars and 11 tracks.

== Gameplay ==
[[File:Hot Wheels Ultimate Racing Gameplay.jpeg|thumb|360x360px|Gameplay of Ultimate Racing on Metropolis]]
Hot Wheels Ultimate Racing features 26 vehicles based on Hot Wheels toy cars. The game features 11 courses, each one resembling real Hot Wheels toy racetracks. The courses are divided across four areas: [[Death Valley]], [[Jungle]], [[Metropolis]], and [[Volcano]]. Each level features a major trap or enemy that must be avoided, such as giant boulders, a giant scorpion, and a giant octopus. The player can use turbo boosts to speed up in races, and slow-motion to safely drift around corners; both abilities are depleted as they are used, and can be refilled by landing specific giant jumps or by avoiding the traps and enemies in each level. Performance upgrades, including better acceleration, improved handling, and new tires, can be won from races.

Hot Wheels Ultimate Racing features four gameplay modes. In Quick Race, the player may choose any track on which to race. In Survival mode, the player must win races that become increasingly difficult. In Time Trial mode, the player must race against a time limit. In Collector mode, the player is the sole vehicle and must collect golden medals scattered around a racetrack. The game also includes a local multiplayer mode for up to four people.

Hot Wheels World:
[[File:HotWheelsWorld.png|200px|right]] Hot Wheels World sets, which began selling in 1997 as the successor to [[Hot Wheels Street Traxx|Street Traxx]], [[Hot Wheels Sto & Go|Sto & Go]] and [[Auto City|Hot Wheels Auto City]], are part of a Hot Wheels track system designed to look like a futuristic city. They have track called "E-Z Snap" that is used for making the owner's track their dream city. From 1997 to around 1999, the sets made were normal and realistic with some stunt elements sprinkled in, then around 2000, sets like the ''Powershift Garage'' and ''Crash Test'' started the trend of Hot Wheels World-compatible sets focusing on stunts and crashes more than an actual city. In late 2003, some Hot Wheels World sets were re-released under the short-lived "Heat Street" (usually shown as "HEAT ST." on a street sign/skyline logo) banner, like the 2001 McDonald's, Jet Port, Copter Chase, etc. These "Heat Street" sets are most likely from outside of the US. The last Hot Wheels World-compatible set was the ''Drag Strip Duel'', or ''Speedtrap Raceway'', released in 2005. These sets were discontinued as of December 2005, but sold in stores until they ran out and could not restock. Over the years, even back when Hot Wheels World sets were still available in stores, Mattel has re-released some Hot Wheels World sets, some examples being the 1997 set ''Car Crusher'' in 2003, 2005 and January 2011, the 1997 set ''Ford Dealership'' in 2005 as ''Auto Showroom'', the 1998 set ''Cement Loading Dock'' in 2005 as ''Nitrox Mine'', and the 2000 set ''Gas Station'' as ''Turbo Garage'' in 2005. Many playsets from the Hot Wheels World and Hot Wheels Heat Street line were later reissued as part of the Turbo Town line as late as 2005 until the final sets from that line were released in 2013, reissues of Crash Curve and Radical Roadway. Jaguar Classic Sportscar 4-Car Set:
In 1998, three vintage Jaguars sold at auctions for sums totaling over $2.8 million. Now, Hot Wheels Collectibles offers you the chance to purchase four classic Jaguars for considerably less.

Officially, Jaguar began in 1922 as the Swallow Sidecar Company. The fledgling enterprise produced cars using parts and subassemblies from several British manufacturers. This production technique limited their ability to effect styling and performance, so in 1935 Swallow produced its first car from the ground up. Their new car needed a name that embodied speed and agility, and Jaguar fitted the bill. In '37 the chrome mascot was added to the hoods and Jaguar was on its way to becoming a premier manufacturer of luxury sports cars.

We have replicated four models which represent milestones in Jaguar styling and technology. From the XJ-13 - a one of a kind 12 cylinder concept car to the rare 1957 XKSS of which only 16 were built, to the classic XKE - the dream sports car of the '60s and '70s, to the latest beauty to carry the Jaguar legacy into the new millennium - the XKR! Each highly detailed model captures the essence of these world-class British sports cars.

Hot Wheels id:
[[File:A5C6D4E1-1BEE-4BBA-9E7A-C5ECB634D2BA.jpeg|thumb|The Hot Wheels id logo|226x226px]]The '''Hot Wheels id''' Series features cars embedded with NFC microchips that originally combined with [[Hot Wheels id (app)|app]]s and customizable Smart Track sets to play a multitude of games. The id Race Portal paired with the app recorded progress for each car. The portal also connects to regular Hot Wheels track. All cars sport full deco, Spectraflame paint, and exclusive [[ID|id wheels]]. Several castings of scale models were retooled for track use. The id system was developed by [[Gerry Cody]] and Ron Friedman. The series was canceled in 2022 due to low sales, overproduction, and the license for the chips ending. Japanese Red Box:
In the late 1970's in Japan, Hot Wheels were sold and packaged in numbered red cardboard boxes. The 'Japan/Japanese Red Box' vehicles are identical to their regular counterparts, but the inclusion of the original packaging makes them hard to find and desirable. Although they are only numbered up to 80, a total of 89 vehicles were packaged this way.

There were two versions of the box, both had the Mattel Logo and 'ミニカ' (minika/minica). Some had a picture of the car with a printed number, and others had no picture but did have a small white box into which the number was stamped. On some vehicles, the picture was different to the actual one inside (example: Red Box #69 had an image of the [[Spoiler Sport]] in pink, while the vehicle inside was green).

Sometimes different versions of the same vehicle could be found in the box. For instance; Red Box #76 [[T-Totaller]] could be either the Black or Brown version, or a vehicle could come with [[RL2|Redline]] or [[BW|Blackwall]] Wheels.

International Mail-Ins:
Mattel Exclusive cars are Hot Wheels, which were sent directly from Mattel to their customers. The Mattel Exclusive Series is a Hot Wheels series in Germany.

For the '''International Gold Editions''' click [[International Gold Editions|'''HERE''']]

==[['65 Volkswagen Fastback]] (2009 Mail In car)==
[[File:GermanpromaFastback.jpg|300px|German version of the Fastback]]
==='''The promotion'''===
In the Summer of 2009 Mattel Germany started the first Mail In car.
For every 10 barcodes you'll get one of the 5.000 free [['65 Volkswagen Fastback|VW Fastbacks]] from Mattel on long card and in a [[Kar Keeper]]. If you sent 20 barcodes you'll get 2 Fastback and so on.
It was limited until end of December 2009.

Also appeared in America as a [[2009 Collector Edition|Toys-R-Us exclusive Mail in]] 


==='''The car'''===
The car was the [['65 Volkswagen Fastback]] in the same variation like the US-car, but the card was a bit different. The US had the writing "Collectors Edition 2009" on the HW-Logo and the German one doesn't have this.
On the back of the German Fastback stands:
"Bitte für mögliche Rückfragen aufbewahren. German Mattel address, Swiss Mattel address, Austrian Mattel address. Nicht zum Gebrauch mit allen Hot Wheels Sets geeignet. Copyrights and licences."


==='''Problems'''===
The most Fastbacks in Germany has a damaged blister. On the left side of the blister is a hole which was caused by the wing from the VW Fastback.

==International Gold Series (2014- Present)==

Starting in 2014, Europe has had Mail-ins promotions for cars to exclusively have Gold variations. For more info check out [[International Gold Editions|'''International Gold Editions''']]

==[[Rev Rod]] (2015 Mail In car)==

[[File:HW Rev Rod 1.jpg|300px]]

==='''The promotion'''===
In the first quarter of 2015 Mattel Europe held another Mail In promotion. This time the promotion car was a special Chrome Black [[Rev Rod]]. After purchasing 4 Hot Wheels cars and send the receipt to Mattel ''before'' May 4<sup>th</sup> 2015, you were send a special Rev Rod on a long card (in The Netherlands the car was detached from its card and sent in an envelope). In every promotion flyer there was a special code. After registering that code, you were send 2 free tickets to the AutoRAI in Amsterdam, The Netherlands, by mail.

==='''The car'''===
The 2015-promotion car is a special, Chrome Black [[Rev Rod]]. This color variation does not appear in the (pre-)2015 mainline and is exclusive to the Mail In. On the back of the card is a multi-angle computer graphic along with the usual safety concerns and so.

==='''Store Exclusive Display''' ===
Selected Dutch stores received an special promotion package. This consisted of the flyers and a box in the form of a picture frame with the Chrome Black Rev Rod centered in it. The box reads: "Wil je ook zo'n EXCLUSIEVE HOT WHEELS AUTO? Bij aanschaf van 4 die-cast Hot Wheels auto's, ontvang je deze GRATIS!!!" Which translates to: "Would you also like one of those EXCLUSIVE HOT WHEELS CARS? When purchasing 4 Die-Cast Hot Wheels cars, it will be send to you, for FREE!!!"

Hot Wheels Railroad:
[[File:HotWheelsRailroad.png|300px|right]]'''Hot Wheels Railroad''' was a very short-lived series of model trains intended to be compatible with Hot Wheels vehicles. These were produced from 1983 to 1985 and were approximately 1/64 scale. The trains were advertised as being "kid-powered" and were compatible with a proprietary type of Hot Wheels track; this track was similar to HO scale track and these trains can work on regular HO scale track. All locomotives were based on real-life trains and featured authentic liveries mimicking real-life railroads.

Steam, diesel and electric locomotives were made available, along with freight cars and cabooses. These coupled to each other using a fork-styled coupler. The locomotives were available singly, in bundles and in larger playsets such as the [[Freight Yard]] and the [[Superrails Station]]. The trains featured plastic bodies and were manufactured in Hong Kong; the tracks were manufactured in the United States and were made in straight, curve, switch and transition (track to floor) pieces. Most rolling stock feature some form of special feature.

Despite the discontinuation of the series, the trains lived on until the 1990s with the [[Sto & Go]] Trucks & Trains Freight Yard, City Trains To Go, and Superrails Station, essentially a rerelease of the old Freight Yard, Trains to Go, and Superrails Station playsets. Some products were sold in Canada, with the line being marketed under the name '''Le Chemin de Fer''' (lit. "the railroad").

Hot Wheels Rims Series:
"Let your size be known!

Rims brand of wheels are the first and only to display the size of your wheel right on the center cap. So there's no guessin' that you'll be rollin' strong."

==Description==
Only out in [[2005]] the Hot Wheels Rims series is a series of Hot Wheel cars decked in the best brand of rims based on actual Rims brand. In the normal Rims series, each Hot Wheels car would be in an oil can case with a big Rim included in the package. The Rims Deluxe version featured a nice acrylic box display to showcase the car and the giant Rim in all angles.  All were made in Thailand.

[[File:HyperCyclesLogo.jpeg|center|300px]]

==Description==
'''Hyper Cycles''' was a series of larger scale gyroscope powered bikes that first debuted in [[1988]]. The first lineup consisted of four single packs and one play set release. This series was renamed '''Hyper-Cycles''' then '''Hyper Wheels''' for later releases.

Releases of the later [[Rev Tredz]] series utilised the same gyroscopes and some modified toolings from the Hyper Cycles series.

Leap Year Models:
A '''leap year''' (also known as an ''intercalary year'' or a ''bissextile year'') is a year containing one additional day added to keep the calendar year synchronized with the astronomical or seasonal year. Because seasons and astronomical events do not repeat in a whole number of days, calendars that have the same number of days in each year drift over time with respect to the event that the year is supposed to track. By inserting (also called intercalating) an additional day into the year, the drift can be corrected. A year that is not a leap year is called a common year. In the Gregorian calendar, each leap year has 366 days instead of the usual 365, by extending February to 29 days rather than the common 28. This page lists the Leap Year models made by Hot Wheels. Kar Keepers:
A '''Kar Keeper''', commonly known as a '''protector''' or a '''plastic casing''', is a plastic case designed to protect and display [[Hot Wheels]], for the collector to keep their Hot Wheels safe for collecting. They are designed to fit all Hot Wheels basic cars and Hot Wheels Classics. In 2007 Mattel came out with another line of Kar Keepers for those collectors collecting [[Ultra Hots Series (2006/2007)|Ultra Hots]], which have a larger card than your basic Hot Wheels card. These larger Kar Keepers also fit the larger cards used for the [[Dragstrip Demons]] series.

A '''Kar Keepers Exclusive''' is a term that is used by the collector that is exclusively through a Department store, or through [[HotWheelsCollectors.com]] in the Shopping Tab, issued by [[Mattel]], and came in a Pack of 10. A '''True Protective clear clamshell''', or '''Kar Keeper''' will have a '''Hot Wheels''' logo embossed in the back of the sleeve. Looney Tunes Character Cars:
The Looney Tunes is an American animated series of short comedy films produced by Warner Bros. The so-called "shorts" were released from 1930 to 1969 during the golden age of American animation. It was known for introducing such famous cartoon characters as Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Porky Pig, Tweety Bird, Sylvester the Cat, Yosemite Sam, Marvin the Martian, Speedy Gonzales, Wile E. Coyote and the Road Runner, the Tasmanian Devil, and many others. These characters themselves are commonly referred to as the "Looney Tunes".

The '''Looney Tunes Character Car series''' consists of 6 different models that were launched in January 2017. The Looney Tunes have also been featured in the Pop Culture series in [[Pop Culture#Looney Tunes|2013]], [[Pop Culture#Looney Tunes 2|2014]] and they have been featured in the [[Looney Tunes Series (2018)|2018 Looney Tunes series]].

John D'Agostino Kustoms 2-Car Set:
In 2002, Hot Wheels replicated two custom cars by car-builder John D'Agostino in the [[100% Hot Wheels]] '''John D'Agostino Kustoms 2-Car Set'''. This set was the first release for the [[1953 Biarritz|'53 Biarritz]] casting.

[[File:JohnDAgSetFront.JPG|500px]]

John D'Agostino's kustom kars have been winning major awards for over three decades. This 100% Hot Wheels 2-car set honors John by replicating two classic models, each having contributed greatly to his Hall of Fame status.

"Marilyn" is John's '53 Cadillac Biarritz convertible that won the World's Most Beautiful Custom and the Goodguy's Custom D'Elegance awards in 1998. The car was inspired by a certain Hollywood blonde beauty and was eventually sold at the Pebble Beach auction for $150,000. That's what we call star billing.

The '57 Eldorado add to John's legend. Its long, sleek body was created by lowering the roof and modifying the rear tailfins. From its sparkling custom chrome grille to the '59 taillights in its split rear bumper, this is one cool car and another gem in John D'Agostino's brilliant career.

Lead Sledz 2-Car Sets:
==2001 Lead Sledz 2-Car Set==

[[File:Lead Sledz 2-Car Sets .JPG|thumb|500px|left]]


For those who are new to the custom car culture, the term 'lead sled' may be puzzling, but to the "crazy" creators of these cool cars, it means chopping the roofs, dropping the bodies and heating up the lead. Manufacturer's emblems and logos are removed, chrome accents and other unwanted applications are stripped off and the remaining holes are filled with lead.

Perhaps the most notable cars in the history of customs for the lead sled treatment were the '49 Mercurys.

Hot Wheels offers you two Mercs, each bearing a flat paint job with glossy flames. We think you'll like our hot and heavy metal.

Lowrider Magazine 3-Car Set:
[[FIle:.. Lowrider Magazine .. SSO8a.jpg|500px]]

The lowrider phenomenon originated in the barrios of Southern California during the late 1940's. This unique folk art quickly spread throughout the communities of the Southwest and into the northern cities of Chicago and Detroit, where it gained national attention and popularity.

Lowriders are not about speed and muscle, but style and beauty. Each one is a hand-crafted artistic expression requiring months and years of dedication and commitment. They have been lifted and lowered. Hydraulics have been added, factory paint removed and replaced with custom hand-rubbed finishes. All in the quest for a one-of-a-kind vehicle.

Our collection of "caliente" cars includes a '53 Chevy Bel Air, a '69 Buick Riviera and a '70 Chevy Monte Carlo. We think they are three of the hottest bombas ever to slam the boulevard!

Legends: Barris Kustom 4-Car Set:
[[File:Barris Kustom 4-Car Set.JPG|center|800px]] In [[1998]], [[Hot Wheels]] commemorated the Legendary custom car shop: Barris Kustoms. Four castings were included based on real-life 'Barris Kustom' vehicles. '''BARRIS KUSTOM:''' ''Where Kustom Is Spelled with a "K"
George and Sam Barris were miles ahead of custom car builders when they opened the Barris Kustom bodyshop in Southern California in the postwar '40s. Their extreme designs and custom craftsmanship influenced the '50s custom car scene and earned them the title "Kings of Kustomizing". It wasn't long before Hollywood took notice and made stars of their flamboyant cars. After Sam passed away in 1967, George continued producing hundreds of award-winning showstoppers and fantasy movie cars more famous than the stars, In the world of showbiz, the Barris crest is the mark of a Hollywood legend. ==Vehicles== The following vehicles were included in the '''[[Legends|Legends: Barris Kustom 4-Car Set]]''': {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size: 85%; text-align: left;" width="95%" ! style="border-style: none none solid solid; background:" |'''Casting Name''' ! style="border-style: none none solid solid; background:" |'''Color''' ! style="border-style: none none solid solid; background:" |'''Photo''' |- |[['51 Merc|Hirohata Merc]] |Light Green |[[File:HirohataMerc100%.jpg|100px|center]] |- |[[Ala Kart]] |White |[[File:AlaKart.jpg|center|100px]] |- |[['49 Merc (100%)|Kustom Merc]] |Red |[[File:BarrisMerc.jpg|100px|center]] |- |[[Elvis Cadillac]] |Gold |[[File:ElvisCadillac.jpg|100px|center]] |} [[Category:1998 Hot Wheels]] [[Category:Hot Wheels by Series]] [[Category:100% Hot Wheels Box Sets]] [[Category:4-Packs]]

[[File:LavaLand Logo.png|center|thumb|300x300px|The Lava Land series logo featuring the four main antagonist, well if you can call a volcano a "antagonist"]]
'''Lava Land''' is a short lived series in [[2004]] of 5 different tribal themed Playsets that could be combined to create "Lava Land"

Hot Wheels made a game on the Hot Wheels website named "Lava Land Jungle Jam"

[[Image:Lava Land sets.JPG|300px]]

==Known Playsets==

===== Volcano Blast =====
[[File:Volcano Blast.JPG|thumb|300x300px]]
''Set Number: B5663''

'''Volcano Blast''' is the first set in the '''Lava Land''' series. It is the smallest set that comes with an exclusive [[Seared Tuner]].

In the set, you can put your car on a lift, a Excavator Bucket hits your car down a ramp, and at the end of the lift, the car will hit a button that activates the "lava" to erupt. There is a parking spot that can "refill" the cars at well.

===== Trivia =====

* On the back of the box, the exclusive [[Seared Tuner]] and the [[T-Bird Stocker (1997)]] are seen as well as the mysterious [[Volcano Blast Concept Car]].

===== Tiger Terror =====
''Set Number: B5667''
[[File:Tiger Terror set.jpg|thumb|320x320px]]
'''Tiger Terror''' is the second set in Lava Land series. It includes no vehicles in any of it's releases.

In the set, the vehicle of your choice will travel across a gravity drop piece molded as a wooden bridge. This piece can be picked up and used as a ramp for the vehicle to go through a giant rock in the shape of a giant tiger head. The tiger has a system that can either bite a vehicle and stop it or let the vehicle pass through without getting crunched. If the vehicle achieves the latter, it will continue on to jump over a snake pit and a ring of fire.

===== Trivia =====

* [[File:Unproduced Tiger Terror Super Tsunami.png|thumb|The unreleased Power Pro seen on the back.]]An unreleased yellow version of [[Super Tsunami|Power Pro]] was seen on the back of the box of the Tiger Terror set. It is assumed and highly likely it was meant to be exclusive to the set but was cancelled for unknown reasons.

Key Force:
[[File:Keyforce Logo.jpg|right|200px]]'''Key Force''' was a short-lived series of transforming vehicle toys produced from [[1992]] to [[1994]]. Each vehicle featured two different modes, which could be unlocked using a key provided with each vehicle. Once the vehicles were transformed, the keys could be inserted into slots in the car's bodies to fire missiles or activate various parts. The keys included with each of the vehicles is unique and may not be used on another vehicle. In 1993, a sub-series, '''Key Force Warriors''', was introduced. The vehicles in this series were somewhat similar to that of ''[[wikipedia:Transformers|Transformers]]'', with each vehicle transforming into a robot. To build on the hype, a few vehicles were released for [[McDonald's]] promotions. ==Narrative== The series, set in 2005, focused on two teams, the Keymasters and the War-Locks, who were trying to wrest control of a city; these were the heroic and evil teams, led by [[Keymmander]] and [[Headlock (Key Force)|Headlock]] respectively. Both teams were trying to wrest control of power keys located throughout the city; the keys's powers would be neutralized if both were together, but the evil keys would turn to be significantly more powerful if separated. The backs of the packaging of each of the vehicles shows the reports of the Keymasters and War-Locks ambushing each other as they performed their tasks to obtain keys for their purposes, with each of them reporting to their leader on the events that occured at the time. Two years after the initial events, the Keymasters and War-Locks begin constructing Warriors, large automatons built to aid the teams in their tasks. Significantly larger than the vehicles, Warriors feature superior strength, size and intelligence compared to their vehicle counterparts. Keymmander activated his Warriors without much testing in an effort to combat Headlock's Warriors, which had already been activated in his attempt to take over the city. ===Chronology of known events=== *21 March 2005, 1100: [[Blade Raider (Key Force)|Blade Raider]] scouts a high rise building for keys using a remotely-controlled helicopter; helicopter opens fire on various Keymasters, who return fire and damage Blade Raider, who requires repairs. *21 March 2005, 1115: [[Rocket Shot (Key Force)|Rocket Shot]] attempts to save [[Swingshot]] being held for ransom by the War-Locks. *21 May 2005, 0000: Headlock mobilizes additional War-Locks to take over the city. *21 May 2005, 1200: Keymmander mobilizes additional Keymasters to stop War-Locks. *12 August 2005, 0900: Swingshot is ambushed by War-Locks near a cave and requests for urgent aerial support. *12 August 2005, 0905: [[Cutthroat]] corners Swingshot at a cliff near the cave and requests for reinforcements. *31 October 2005, 2300: [[Road Kill (Key Force)|Road Kill]] attempts to obtain keys in a museum but is ambushed by one of Keymmander's traps; he then retreats to a cemetery to get ready to strike Keymmander. *5 December 2005, 0700: [[Jet Threat (Key Force)|Jet Threat]] is ambushed by War-Locks in an abandoned auto factory, gets hit and requires repairs. *14 April 2007, 2302: Headlock mobilizes [[Dark Shield]] to aid in his quest to defeat the Keymasters. *14 April 2007, 2305: Headlock mobilizes [[Pulverider]] to aid in his quest to defeat the Keymasters. *15 April 2007, 0103: Keymmander mobilizes [[Enforcer (Key Force)|Enforcer]] in response to Headlock's recent mobilizations. *15 April 2007, 0105: Keymmander mobilizes [[White Heat]] in response to Headlock's recent mobilizations without much prior testing. ==Products== ===Key Force=== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size: 100%; text-align: left" width="80%" ! LionChief:
[[File:LionChiefLogo.jpeg|right|300px]]'''LionChief''' is an entry-level product line manufactured by [[Lionel|Lionel, LLC]]. Trains in this line are O gauge trains done to semi-scale proportions, featuring reduced detailing compared to Lionel's other offerings and a simpler control system using a plastic handheld remote; trains in this scale are incompatible with Lionel's other command control systems. Later iterations of the system, known as '''LionChief Plus''' and '''LionChief Plus 2.0''', feature improved functionality, with the latter being compatible with Lionel's TMCC control system while retaining all of LionChief's other features.

Hot Wheels released a sub-series in [[2018]] to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Hot Wheels. It consisted of various branded O gauge models and accessories.  

A contest ran from 13 August 2018 to 24 August 2018 on the Lionel Trains Facebook page where a single participant was chosen to win a free copy of the [[Electric O-Gauge Train Set]].

M&D Toys Limited Edition:
==Description==
In the 1990s, Hot Wheels collecting was staring to flourish. The kids who collected Hot Wheels back in the Redline era are now adults trying to collect every car. It wasn't until the 1990's that Hot Wheels would release special Limited Edition cars that had a much limited release than the usual mainline car. One could say this was a precursor to the [[Treasure Hunt]] cars.

The name of these cars is a bit confusing since most of them simply say "Limited Edition", then "Limited RCN Collectors Edition" and finally "M&D Toys Limited Edition". "M&D Toys" means '''M'''ichael Strauss (author of the [[Tomart's Price Guide Exclusives]]) & '''D'''iane Strauss (his wife and editor of the HW Newsletter). And just like any set/series, these cars have a list on the back of the Blister that list more cars as time went on, grouping all these cars below:

[[File:Kit_Racing_Logo.png|center|300px]]
==Description==
'''K.I.T. Racing''' or '''Kinetic Interactive Technology Racing''' is a series of 1/64 scale motorized vehicles designed by [[Takara Tomy]] that first debuted in [[2002]]. Each model includes separate parts (Heat Sinks, Guide Rollers, Motor, Body, Suspension, Base/Chassis, Axles, Transfer Gears, Tires, Weights, and Wings) that change four defined categories of track performance on the model they are applied; Top Speed, Sustained Power, Acceleration, and Handling. Extra blisters of parts were available alongside a single track set. This series originally debuted as “Tomica Bit Racer” on February 17, 2001 in Japan; it was scrapped due to lack of interest and pitched by [[Jeremy Padawer]] under [[Hot Wheels]] which he described as "disastrous" due to scaring Kroger buyers with a "mad scientist" impression.  

''This series is known to have issues with brittle and crumbling parts due to age''

McDonald's:
'''History''' Since June 1979, McDonald's has developed promotions for children with small plastic toys in their '''Happy Meals'''. The first diecast cars distributed for '''McDonald's''' started in 1983, using the regular [[Hot Wheels]] mainline models, which continued up to 1990. In 1991 '''McDonald's''' started distributing their own car designs in''' Happy Meals''' for the first time in plastic baggies within the Happy Meal box (as opposed to full blisterpack cards). In the early years of the "baggie cars", these cars were usually cheaper plastic-bodied versions of mainline Hot Wheels that were sold at retail at the time of release, but this eventually changed to cars designed specifically for McDonald's Happy Meals by the start of the millenium. Most Hot Wheels promotions at McDonald's restaurants mainly have a Barbie promotion as well for the girls side. Megaforce Series:
[[File:MegaforceLogo.png|200px|right]]
'''''Megaforce''''' is an action film made in 1982 directed by former stuntman [[wikipedia:Hal Needham|Hal Needham]]. Mattel released a special series of Hot Wheels cars that corresponded to the movie that same year; all were made in Hong Kong. The vehicles in the movie were designed in collaboration with Mattel. Only the [[Enforcer|Megadestroyer]] castings were actually new; the rest were either retooled or repurposed from previous releases. All castings with the exception of the [[Tac-Com]] would see further rereleases under different names. All castings feature copyright information pertaining to a "North Shore Investments, Ltd." Although the series uses Hot Wheels models, this series are not branded as Hot Wheels.

Not to be confused with the 2013 season of Power Rangers, [[Power Rangers Megaforce]], which had its own Hot Wheels line of Character Cars.

Mechanix:
{{stub}} Mechanix was a series that featured cars and other vehicles which could be customized with interchangeable parts. Each set contained one vehicle, a tool and some parts like monster truck wheels, bumpers and spoilers that could be added to or removed from the vehicle easily. The first set was released in 1997. In the next year, the "Mechanix Deluxe" line appeared, where two vehicles, like a Plane & a Car, could be merge together. Maniacs:
[[File:Maniacs Logo.png|right|150x150px]]
'''Maniacs''' was a short-lived series of very large-scale interactive Hot Wheels cars produced from 2007 to 2008. The cars in said series featured LCD screens which would project their drivers on them; the player could then engage in a series of rather crude minigames using the buttons on the hood, or interact with the car by spinning it around, smashing the front bumpers or doing other actions. [[Kevin Cao]] and [[Alton Takeyasu]] are known to have worked on this line, with Cao being a project lead. Ron Yavnieli animated some of the screens.

The series was not successful and was discontinued after a year, likely because parents would usually never approve of their kids playing around with toys producing such crude humor. Only two products were released before the series was permanently discontinued.

Micro Hot Wheels:
'''Micro Hot Wheels '''is a series of miniature Hot Wheel cars that came out in [[1989]] to compete with the newest phenomenon of diecast toys "[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micro_Machines Micro Machines]". They are the first series for Hot Wheels to venture into making cars smaller than their usual 1:64 scale. After the series ended within a year (or two?), Hot Wheels would later venture again into the micro cars in series like [[Hot Wheels Micro Vehicles]], [[Planet Micro]], [[Atomix]], [[Micro Madnetics]] & [[Worlds Smallest Hot Wheels]]. In [[1990]] they where renamed to the '''Mini Hot Wheels''' but came with the same and new castings. One thing to note, even though the Micro Hot Wheels where smaller than normal Hot Wheels, they where bigger than [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micro_Machines Micro Machines], which later series corrected. Micro Vehicles:
After the [[Micro Hot Wheels]] line, the '''Hot Wheels Micro Vehicles''' came out as a replacement in 1996 for a year (or two?) to fill the micro scale diecast slot. These unique cars have a hook on the front and a hole in the back, allowing collectors to hook cars together, make "a rope of cars", or race the micro cars down a track similar to a roller coaster carts. Minecraft Mini-Figures:
[[File:Minecraft_logo.png|center|300px]]
==Description==
'''Minecraft Mini-Figures''' is a [[Mattel]]-branded series of rubber-plastic figures and sets based off the [[Minecraft]] license that first debuted in [[2014]] through blind boxes. [[Hot Wheels]] has released multiple compatible track sets designed by [[Neal Smith]], [[Jason Liu]], and [[Design Team|many others]] since [[2016]]. A perspective distanced half inch "grid system" was developed for scale consistency in prototyping; all final releases included the [[Minecart]] casting. The segment Track Blocks (conceptualized as Stunt Block) was introduced in [[2017]] featuring intersecting angled tracks. Later releases were compatible with the [[Hot Wheels City]] system. An Ender Dragon set was planned but went unreleased due to series cancellation in [[2018]].

Mattel Brick Shop:
[[File:MattelBrickShop.jpg|100px|right]]'''Mattel Brick Shop''' is a toy line introduced in [[2025]] featuring interlocking plastic bricks similar to LEGO. The sets feature an exclusive miniature model with a metal signature plate; each buildable car features swappable parts for customization. Similar to the [[MEGA Showcase Hot Wheels|MEGA Showcase]] line, the cars in the series are replicated in different scales and have different part counts; three tiers of vehicles are available, those being Premium, Elite and Speed. Premium sets come with a high-end miniature in a display case, Elite vehicles come with a premium or [[Themed assortment|semi-premium]] miniature and Speed vehicles come with a [[mainline|basic]] miniature. Mystery Cars:
= Mail In Mystery Cars =

The Mystery Cars were originally a Hot Wheels mail in offer in which the car received was left a mystery. In 2005, as part of the 10th Anniversary Treasure Hunt celebration, Mattel offered four mystery cars, each car came with a voucher. Collecting all four vouchers was required to obtain an exclusive 13th [[Treasure Hunts|Treasure Hunt]] [[Volkswagen Drag Bus]]. The four vouchers form a picture of the Drag Bus. Randomly a 13/12 Treasure Hunt #133 was Ramdomly sent/received with a "Antique PATINA Base" vari and no Voucher card included.

=Black Blister Mainline Segments=
2007 saw mystery cars introduced to the mainline. These are identified by a [http://4toycars.com/photos/MAT64-L2593.m.jpg black stripe] that runs the length of the right side of the [[card]], extending from the top of the card to the bottom of the card. On this stripe, there will be white writing that reads '''MYSTERY'''. 

There has been a great amount of speculation about decoding the numbers on the mystery cars to identify what is inside. Until 2010 the only way to see any of the car inside was to open them. This has resulted in a rash of packages being opened in the stores. The 2010 Mystery packaging includes a small hole in the back to help mitigate this problem.

Monster Duo:
Released in 2008, the '''Monster Duos''' matched Monster Jam Trucks with Hot Wheels Vehicles. The original 3 releases were. [[Hot Wheels (Monster Jam)|Hot Wheels]] paired with [[Off Track]], [[Captain's Curse]] paired with [[Jaded]], & [[Monster Mutt]] paired with [[Purple Passion]].

The Duos returned in 2010 with all 3 original releases re-issued.

Then in 2011, the series returned with new  Advanced AutoParts [[Monster Jam]] logos which make both vehicles unique variants.

*The Monster Duos were issued in groups of 3, All 3 in a group shared a common card with a common Toy #

Mystery Models:
[[File:MysteryModels.png|300px|right]]'''Mystery Models''' were released in early November 2011 across [[Wal-Mart]] stores in the United States. These vehicles came in foil packs similar to trading cards, as opposed to [[Mystery Cars]] which came on blister cards with blackened out bubbles. Codes on the back of the packs can be used to determine what model one would get.

From 2026 onwards, the Mystery Models series now primarily consists of re-releases of previous mainlines (occasionally featuring minor revisions), with only the first 3 cars in each mix being unique to the series. Prior to this, they largely featured unique decos/colors, with each individual mix revolving around a set theme (often overlapping between series, particularly between 2018-2025).

Monster Jam:
[[Image:MonsterJam.jpeg|right|250px]]

The Hot Wheels Monster Jam license was a long-standing partnership between Mattel’s '''Hot Wheels''' brand and '''Monster Jam''', the premier monster truck entertainment series. Through this collaboration, which began in '''2000''' and lasted until '''2018''', Hot Wheels produced a wide range of officially licensed Monster Jam products, including:

* '''Monster Trucks''' (primarily in 1:64, 1:43 and 1:24 scales)
* '''Playsets''' featuring stunt tracks, ramps, and arenas
* '''Feature Vehicles''' with special designs and moving parts
* '''Accessories''' and collectibles inspired by Monster Jam events

During the partnership, Hot Wheels replicated many of the most iconic trucks from the Monster Jam circuit while also creating original designs known as "Hot Wheels Originals." Some of these originals remained exclusive to the toy line, while others were later brought to life as real Monster Jam trucks.

The license allowed Hot Wheels to play a significant role in shaping the Monster Jam brand, with Mattel designers contributing creative truck designs and concepts. The toys became highly collectible, especially in the 1:64 scale, which remains a fan favorite.

In '''2018''', the partnership between Hot Wheels and Monster Jam ended, and the license transitioned to Spin Master, which now produces official Monster Jam products. However, Hot Wheels continues to release monster truck toys under their own [[Hot Wheels Monster Trucks]] line, featuring both original designs and new concepts.

== 1/87 Scale Monster Trucks==
In [[2003]] a series of small scale Monster Jam trucks came out in the Speed Demons series. These are pull back powered plastic trucks. The series includes various designs and variations, which can be explored in more detail [[Speed_Demons_Series_(2003)#HW_Monster_Jam|HERE]]

In [[2017]] a series of small scale Monster Jam trucks came out in the [[Monster Jam Mighty Minis]] series. They do not use the same castings as those in the [[Speed Demons]] series. Each truck comes with a key, and pressing the buttons on its sides launches the Mini Monster Truck.

To honor the company whose unmistakable eyes have become an icon in the rod and custom car culture, Mattel has created the '''Moon Equipped Truck set'''. Two highly detailed haulers bearing Dean Moon's lovable and loco logo!

Mustang Monthly Magazine 2-Car Set:
[[File:MustangMonthlyMagazineSetFront.JPG|500px]]

100% Hot Wheels proudly joins Mustang Monthly Magazine in presenting this special 2-Car Set celebrating the Ford Mustang and its legions of faithful fans. 

From its highly heralded beginning, the Mustang has always been at the cutting edge of automotive design and technology. Still, it was a jumping-off point for those who placed their personal stamp on the car. 

The Mustang 'look' is often modified, like our sweet '65, and then there were Carroll Shelby's famous performance enhancements on the '67 GT-500.

This Mustang Monthly set reflects an ongoing passion for the 'original' pony car and is designed for the fanatic followers of these fast, fabulous Fords.

Motorized X-V Racers:
[[File:XV racer collage.jpg|right|200x200px]] '''Motorized X-V Racers''' was a series of Hot Wheels cars produced from 1996 to 2000. These were essentially the successors of the [[Sizzlers]] castings, which were motorized and flew about the track at high speeds. Each casting came which a charger known as a Power Base Booster. Some reused names from previous Hot Wheels cars. The series spawned two offshoot series: [[Motorized Kart Maniax]] in 2001 and [[Ferrari X-V]] in 2005. [[File:Kart Maniax Vehicles & Stunt Pit Set- TV Commercial|500px|center]]

'''Motorized Kart Maniax''' was a short-lived series of [[Hot Wheels]] cars that was an offshoot of the [[Motorized X-V Racers]] series. These were introduced in [[2001]] and ran for about a year. These had two gears so they could perform stunts or for speed. Each featured a Kart Charger, which was essentially a Power Base Booster from the X-V Series with a different design. This series was developed by [[Eric Tscherne]].

Modifighters:
[[File:Modifighters.png|200px|right]]'''Modifighters''' was a short-lived Hot Wheels series that was produced only in 2007. The series's gimmicks was their transforming abilities, similar to the ''Transformers'' line of transforming robots. The castings would transform into licensed vehicles and back into robots with a number of articulated points and pivots. The castings would also reveal battle damage if shot at or doused with cold water. Two lines are known to exist: the standard '''Modifighters''' line and the '''Modifighters Quick Changers''' line, which transformed as they rolled along. Several of these models were also found on the Flying Colors cards.

Power Rangers Megaforce:
[[File:Power Rangers Megaforce logo.png|thumb|254x254px]] '''Power Rangers Megaforce '''is a line of specially designed vehicles part of the [[Character Cars]] line to celebrate the 20th Anniversary of Power Rangers. In this line, there are vehicles that are designed after a specific character in the current '''Megaforce '''series. Wave 1 includes 5 new designs as well as one specially decorated [[Drift King]]. Similar to the [[DC Character Cars|DC Comics line]], these vehicles are representations of the Zords from the show, not actually vehicles in the show. There was also a [[Power Rangers Megaforce Action Set|playset]] to go along with these.  The playset features the [[Drift King|Mega Strike Racer]]. Photo Finish 3-Vehicle Set:
[[File:32314738_2.jpg|CENTER|300px]]

This [[100% Hot Wheels|Hot Wheels Collectibles]] Set celebrates the roots of racing. On Saturday nights, at regional raceways, local heroes traveled for miles to race on quarter-mile dirt ovals. They would push their sprint cars through hot laps, time trials, and heat races in a grueling process of elimination, during which the fittest and fastest survived to race in the Main Event. Then, with dirt flying, the cars would slide through the turns - the lead changing two or three times within one lap - and then a final sprint to the championship was decided by a... PHOTO FINISH.

The Photo Finish set, which includes '56 Ford Pickup, trailer, and '60s Sprint Car celebrates the guts and glory of sprint car racing at its finest.

This specially crafted Porsche 50th Anniversary set includes a 550 Roadster. a 930 Turbo, a 917, and a Boxster - each car harboring the soul of its ancestors. Pavement Pounders:
==Description== Pavement Pounders was the name for the second series of transport trucks and included bonus vehicles that ran from late 1999 to 2003, coming after [[Long Haulers]] and before [[Truckin' Transporters]], [[Racing Rigs]], and [[Super Rigs]]. See also [[Kool Toyz Racing Pack]]s, [[Super Race Rigs]] and [[Wild Race Teams]], playsets that included Pavement Pounders. ==1999== Very little information exists regarding this first series of Pavement Pounders. Night Ridin' Sizzlers:
[[File:NightRidin'Sizzlers.png|200px|right]]'''Night Ridin' Sizzlers''' was a short-lived spinoff of the [[Sizzlers]] line introduced in 1978. All castings were molded in pastel colors and featured headlamps which could be turned on or off. At least two playsets, the [[Day/Night Challenge]] and [[Nightmare Alley]], were also produced.

[[File:Screenshot 2022-02-14 200339.png|520px]]

All castings introduced in this series were new castings. This was the last of the original Sizzlers spinoffs and the last of the original Sizzlers as a whole. The line was discontinued in 1978, along with the entire Sizzlers lineup due to failing sales.

[[File:Screenshot 2022-02-14 200803.png|520px]]

[[File:Hot Wheels - Planet Micro Ad 2|500px|center]] '''Planet Micro''' is a series of small scale (approximately 1:150 scale) Hot Wheels in the late 1990s. They came after the the [[Micro Hot Wheels]] and before the [[Atomix]] series. Planet Micro cars are actually smaller than the [[Micro Hot Wheels]] series from the late 80s/ early 90s with the punchline "Micro Size, Mega Detail!" A lot of the vehicles in the series are based on actual 1/64 Hot Wheels castings. There was a pause in the line of these miniature cars, and when they came back in the early 2000s, the series was renamed the [[Atomix]] series which has both new and old castings from the Planet Micro series transferred over. Most of the Planet Micro cars where sold in "Microscape" sets (and possibly randomly found in single sets?). Rescue Team:
The '''Rescue Team''' series was one of seven themes as part of what some call the "Patch Cards".  You could mail in six proofs of purchase and 25 cents for shipping and handling to receive one patch.  These were produced in 1978 and 1979, and all were made in Hong Kong.  Several of these models were also found on the Flying Colors cards.

Revealers:
=='''Description'''== [[File:Revelerspack.JPG|150px]][[File:Revealers_bp_back.jpg|right|135px]] The '''Revealers''' from 1993 were a series of cars with a lottery type of game included. They were the original [[Mystery cars]]. The cars were sold in different clear blister packs, but they were wrapped inside a yellow opaque paper baggie. The baggie was intended to be dissolved in water, but it was easier and less messy to just tear them open. Though the contents of what was inside remains a mystery, the only clue given is the numbers on the wrapping paper. Example; the "11" on the package above suggests that inside is the [[Custom Corvette Convertible]]. Though what color variation, out of three, is unknown until you reveal it! [[File:Revealer_token_blue.jpg|left |150px]] The main purpose of them being packaged this way was because there were a limited number of cars packaged with a plastic Hot Wheels Logo token to be sent in to Mattel for a prize. If you found one with a Blue Logo, then you would send it to Mattel to receive a special [[Box set of 10 Revealers]] Hot Wheels. If you found a Gold Hot Wheels Logo then that was good for a boys 22" Bicycle Decorated in Hot Wheels Team Blue with logos and a Gold Plated [[Lamborghini Countach]] (see below). ==Versions== There were twelve different castings, each released in three different colors. Revvers:
[[File:Revvers.png|200px|right]]Hot Wheels released the Revvers series in '''1973 only'''. They were diecast vehicles that were slightly larger than regular Hot Wheels and when the wheel located at the back of the car was wound up, a button on the bottom would release the tension and they would "rev" along the floor under their own power. The wheel was connected to a rubber band which was connected to a small array of plastic gears connected to the rear axle. It was similar to that of a wooden airplane. There were several models released, including some in two-packs, and even one that resembled a camping trailer. Replica Entertainment:
[[File:ReplicaEntertainment.png|right|200px]]'''Replica Entertainment''' is the final name for a retired [[Hot Wheels Premium|premium]] Hot Wheels series that ran from [[2013]] to [[2023]]. The series features highly-detailed models of vehicles from various films and television properties as well as other forms of media. Several new castings debut in the series, and a few castings appear with a die-cast chassis for the first time. These editions all feature [[Real Riders]] wheels and authentic deco.

The series, when first introduced in 2013, was given the name of '''Retro Entertainment'''; a year later, the series name was changed to '''Hot Wheels Entertainment''', with the series staying with this name until 2017 when it was renamed to its final name of Replica Entertainment.

The series was merged with [[2024 Pop Culture|Pop Culture]] in 2024.

Rod & Custom 2-Car Sets:
==2001 Rod & Custom 2-Car Set==

[[File:RodCustom100Box_%281%29.JPG|500px]]

Hot Wheels Collectibles joins Rod & Custom Magazine in celebrating a classic '60's dynamic duo. Two auto icons from an era in which "custom" was king.

Dean Jeffries' Manta Ray. Winner of the 1964 Oakland Roadster Show, the Manta Ray was the quintessential custom car of the era. Its full-house Cobra motor rested ona Maserati Grand Prix chassic encased in a sleek, handmade aluminum body. Its single-seat cockput was covered by a Plexiglas canopy.

Bob Tindle's Orange Crate. A huge Olds mill, with front-mounted blower produced plenty of juice for this classic '32 Ford 2-door sedan. The Orange Crate feature knock-off wheels, a single seat and a custom paint job that speaks for its self. It's no wonder it raced away as an Oakland Car show winner.

==2002 Rod & Custom 2-Car Set==

[[File:Kkk1.JPG|500px]]

As time and technology take us father and father away from the origins of the custom car culture, it's refreshing to occasionally glance into the rearview mirror and look back to when the seeds of this incredible phenomenon took root.

Long before turn-key custom cruisers changed hands at upscale car shows and hot rod assembly kits became commonplace, dedicated young men on meager budgets would seach junkyards for a piece of chrome, an unusal grille, or stylish taillights. Anything that was cool inexpensive was used to create their unique custom vehicles. Many of those "works-in-progress" hit the road with primer paint jobs.

Our 100% Hot Wheels Rod and Custom Magazine vehicle set celebrates the passion and commitment of those who spent years creating their moving works of art and set the stage for the custom cars of the new century.

[[File:9a.JPG|500px]] When [[Mattel]] began producing 1:64 scale vehicles nearly thirty-five years ago the goal was to build and replicate the world's coolest cars on or off track. RRRumblers:
[[File:RRRumblers.png|right|200px]]'''RRRumblers''' was a fairly short-lived series of [[Hot Wheels]] 1:32 scale motorbikes produced during the [[Redline]] era from [[1971]] to [[1973]]. The selling point of the motorbikes was their ability to run on Hot Wheels track. Each came with a ''Track-Rack'' (a "carriage" with 2 or 4 small transparent wheels) which allowed them to run on Hot Wheels track; the stand could be removed and the motorbikes displayed on their own with their kickstands down. Numerous castings were produced before the line was discontinued in 1973. RRRumblers are noted to be extremely expensive to acquire today. [[File:AD 1972 RRRumblers 33.jpg|center|250px]] This series is not to be confused with the later [[Rumblers]] series from [[2007]] featuring cars with lights and sounds. Robo Wheels:
[[Image:robo.jpeg|200px|right|link=Special:FilePath/Robo.jpeg]]

'''Robo Wheels''' (ロボウィール) was a short-lived series of transforming cars designed by [[Dave Martis]] and [[Steve Turton]] and [[Design Team|many others]] similar to toys like ''Transformers'' and ''GoBots''. Designed as 1/64 scaled cars released under the ''Hot Wheels'' branding, they can easily be transformed into little skate-boarding robots, capitalizing on the late-'90s X-Sports craze. The bottom deck of the car is cast in diecast metal, while the articulated robots and car parts are plastic. The body of the robots make up the engine, and the body parts of the cars attach to the arms or legs. With multiple cars, one can easily customize their Robo Wheels to create the perfect fighter. 

Developed for Bandai by PLEX, (the same people that designed several ''Machine Robo'', ''Super Sentai'', and ''Power Rangers'' toys) ''Robo Wheels'' were intended for a now-defunct Machine Robo revival. Intended for a release between ''CG Robo'' and ''Machine Robo GP'', the plans never came to fruition. 

In 1999, Bandai and Mattel entered into an agreement consolidating their management resources, products, and marketing in an attempt to maximize their global reach and revenues. In Japan, Bandai would market and sell Mattel products under the Bandai brand, and in Latin American markets, Mattel would market and sell Bandai products under ''both'' Mattel and Bandai brand names. 

The plans for the Machine Robo version of Robo Wheels launch were scraped, and Bandai licensed the designs and material to Mattel for a US launch, echoing back to the 1983 Bandai/Tonka licensing agreement that birthed GoBots.

Developed by industry veteran PLEX, who worked with both Bandai and Mattel in the past, Robo Wheels often homaged older super robots and sentai series, many of which PLEX had a hand in designing, such as ''Machine Robo'', ''RoGun'', and most noticeably, ''Bismark''.

The story of Robo Wheels is tried and true. The good Positrons lived on the peaceful, atom-like planet of Positron, skateboarding across the world down some very Hot-Wheels-esk tracks. One fateful day, the Negabotz attacked, infecting some of the Positrons and turning them evil. Their war raged on until it made its way to Earth. 

Released in North American markets in 2001-2002, the story was told through commercials, fiction blurbs on cardback, and a short CGI film entitled [[Robo Wheels Battle Arena: Earth]] distributed as a VHS pack-in. (Although it has a stated runtime of 23 minutes, only 7 minutes and 11 seconds is the actual pilot. The rest of the runtime is dedicated to worldbuilding and character files.)

Wave 1 consisted of 14 figures: 7 Positrons, and 7 Negabotz. The first release also included Tranz-Blaster, a Robo Wheel-carrying spaceship that transforms into a giant robot. It was released in both red and blue, as a Negabotz and a Positrons respectively. Both sets included the same, un-named Robo Wheels figure. The 2001 launch concluded with the Battle Arena playset.

Wave 2 had a ''very'' limited release in 2002. The Color Changers were a mish-mash of themes. 15 figures were designed for Wave 2, subdivided into the previously established Positrons and Negabotz, while introducing a third faction of Neutroids, playing on the atom motif. Wave 2 was subdivided ''again'' into Extreme, Ninja, and Camo designations. All of them had heat-sensitive chromatic paint, changing colors in hot and cold. 

The Crash Coaster playset was released with the only non-articulated, non-transforming Robo Wheels in the line. A static, orange plastic figure permanently attached to his wheelbase, the figure also featured the Wave 2 color-changing features.

Only the Crash Coaster and Ninja Positrons from Wave 2 saw anything close to a normal release. They still sport their Wave 1 cardbacks. The line was summarily canceled partway through 2002. 

Wave 2.5 ran from 2003-2005. Released exclusively in Latin American markets, it consisted of the full release of Wave 2 Robo Wheels, plus the Extreme Half Pipe playset. In an ironic twist, Japan finally saw their domestic release of Wave 1, unchanged from their American release, with the addition of stickers containing Japanese text. The 14-model range retailed for 750 yen each ($6.38).

Robo Wheels sold around two million units in the United States during 2001. Sales expectations were expected to be four million worldwide by March 2003.<ref>https://www.cnn.com/2002/BUSINESS/asia/08/15/japan.bandai/index.html</ref>

Road Rippers:
[[File:RoadRippers.png|200px|right]]'''Road Rippers''' was a line of large-scale vehicle toys featuring lights and sounds manufactured by Toy State Industrial, also known as Nikko Toys. Toy State started producing Hot Wheels-themed vehicles from around 2015 onwards.

Road Rippers depicted vehicles from various other brands, as well as vehicles created using Toy State's own designs. These were available under a number of different "sub-segments", with each "sub-segment" touting a different feature. The line was discontinued when Toy State ceased operations in 2018; some of the products have been rereleased by [[Mondo Motors]] after the Road Rippers line was discontinued.
