Since '68 Series:
[[File:Since68logo.jpg|200px|right]] The '''''Since '68''''' series was released from late 2007 through 2008 to commemorate the fortieth anniversary of Hot Wheels. New models were introduced, including the [[Purple Passion Woody]], the [['64 Dodge 330]] and the [[Custom Mustang Convertible|Custom Ford Mustang Convertible]]. The series included four segments of individually packaged vehicles: ''Top 40'', ''Muscle Cars'' (10), ''Hot Rods'' (10) and ''Originals'' (10). Packaged sets included the ''Collector Top 40'' set (not to be confused with the ''40 Years of Hot Wheels'' set) and four 4-car sets in commemorative tins: two ''Muscle Cars'' sets and one set each of ''Hot Rods'' and ''Originals''. Snap-On Tools Promotions:
[[File:Snap-on.gif|500px]] ==Snap-On Tools Description== [http://www.snapon.com/ Snap-On] Tools is a tool manufacturer and distributor. The company services professional shops by selling the tool line directly to these. They are geared toward the professional and distribute their tools off a truck that makes stops at service center's once or twice a week. Snap-On invented the removable socket, hence the name Snap-On. Before this invention the socket was a one-piece speed wrench, so one was needed for every size (5/16", 7/16", 1/2" etc.). So now users had a speed wrench with removable sockets that snapped on and off. This saved considerable space and weight in the tool box. "Johnson and Seideman created a set of 10 sockets that would ''snap on'' to five different handles. The idea that ''Five Do the Work of Fifty,'' revolutionised the industry and in 1920, the Snap-on Wrench Company was born." Sizzlers:
[[File:Sizzlers.png|right|300px]]'''Sizzlers''' was a line of motorized Hot Wheels cars produced from 1970 to 1978. The line was engineered by [[George Soulakis]], who also recommended the ''TampoPrint'' process to apply tampos on Hot Wheels cars.

==History==
[[File:Sizzlers CIPSA Poster.jpg|right|200px]]
The '''Sizzlers''' were a 1970s Hot Wheels spin off with a built-in motor and a tiny rechargeable battery. They were introduced in 1970 and became an instant smash. Sizzlers run on the regular "orange" Hot Wheels track, and Mattel created special race sets with U-Turns, multi-level spirals and loops to take advantage of the cars' electric motor. Two lane race sets such as the California/8 race set were developed that allowed Sizzlers to race side-by side, until Mattel created the black '''Fat Track''', which is three lanes wide, with steep banked curves, and designed to allow Sizzlers to run free. In action, Sizzlers display a unique, competitive "passing action" when running on the Fat Track, as if each car were piloted by an impatient driver trying to jockey ahead of the rest. The Fat Track sets included the "Big O", "California 500", and Super Circuit" race sets, and accessories such as the "Scramble Start" (a four-car starting gate), "Lap Computer" four car lap counter, and "Race-Timer" stop watch.

Six cars were made in 1970, 12 cars were made in 1971, and 4 cars were made in 1972. The [[Fat Daddy Sizzlers|"Fat Daddy" Sizzlers]] (oversized bodies with huge tires) were introduced in 1973. Mattel put the Sizzlers on a hiatus after that year, and in 1976 they created [[Sizzlers II]]. That next year, the [[Night Ridin' Sizzlers]] (which had headlights you could turn on or off) were created. Because of faded popularity (possibly due to poor marketing), Mattel permanently stopped Sizzlers production in 1978.

Sizzlers were (and are) charged with four or two D battery chargers called the [[Juice Machine (Sizzlers)|Juice Machine]] and [[Goose Pump]] respectively. Later, the [[Power Pit]] was introduced—which was an electric charger that plugged into any household AC outlet and resembled a race track garage or pit stop. A 90-second charge of the tiny internal Ni-Cad battery gives up to five minutes of frenetic run time. It has been said that the 90-second charge time was "the longest minute and a half in a kid's life" as they waited impatiently for the car to charge sufficiently to get back into the race. In [[2007]], the series was rebooted and exclusive to Target.  All were made in China and had [[NCRL]] wheels.  The series was discontinued by 2009.

The Sizzler electric technology spun off into the [[Hot Line]] trains, which ran on track similar to regular Hot Wheels, and the [[Earthshakers]] [[Ground Hog]]. Both series were charged using the Juice Machine or Power Pit.

In the 1990s, toy company Playing Mantis re-released Sizzlers in NASCAR stock car models and reproduced the Fat Track as the "Stocker 400" and "Mach 500" track sets. The Juice machine was renamed the "Mega-Charger" and incorporated a more efficient "trickle charge" rather than the "dump charge" of the original machines. Interest in the Sizzlers line began to increase once again. They were taken off the market after Mattel filed a lawsuit against Playing Mantis. However, Sizzlers returned again in 2007, when Mattel struck an exclusive deal with Target stores to re-release Sizzlers cars, the "Big O" Fat track, Juice Machine and car carrying case—all in the original packaging from the 1970s. As of January 2009, the Sizzlers line has been discontinued by Target.

Scorchers:
[[File:ScorchersLogo.png|right|250px]]'''Scorchers''' were a range of spring-powered [[Hot Wheels]] vehicles designed by [[Mike McKittrick]] and others introduced in [[1979]]. They were not the first motorized cars produced by Hot Wheels; the rechargeable battery-powered [[Sizzlers]] had been introduced in 1969 (although these were not diecast), and the clunky rubber-band powered [[Revvers]] dated from 1973. However, the Scorchers were the first powered diecast cars that actually worked convincingly. A total of twelve castings were made for the series; each casting had two versions, each with a different name. Six castings were introduced in 1979, two in 1980 and four in 1981. The series was discontinued in 1982. Smoke 'N Water 3-Vehicle Set:
[[File:Somke n'Water.jpg|thumb]]
[[File:SMOKE & WATER 1959 CHEVY PU TRAILER & CRACKERBOX BOAT SSO7.jpg|500px]]


It's a perfect summer morning. The sky is clear, the lake is glassy and the temperature is already in the high 70's. A rock 'n' roll classic plays on the radio at the marina as you slowly roll into a stop near the launch ramp. Instantly, a crowd gathers to admire your tricked out tandem. The '59 Chevy Apache Fleetside pickup has been modified for high performance with a 409 cid engine and dual quad carbs. On your trailer is a classic Crackerbox Race Boat, powered by a nail-valve Buick mill with six carburetors. Your vehicle and vessel combine to produce nearly 800 horsepower and your fans have come to watch your boat create smoke on the water.

Shift Kickers:
[[File:ShiftKickers.png|200px|right]]'''Shift Kickers''' was a short-lived series of Hot Wheels cars produced only in 1983. The selling point of the cars was their "stick shift" action; each of the cars had a comically oversized shifter which sort of acted as a handbrake. Pulling back the handle locks the wheels in place and makes the car unable to move; pushing the handle forwards allows the car to go. The series was discontinued in 1984.

All castings were modified from [[Scorchers]] castings. These castings are now extremely hard to come by, with most loose examples being found in poor condition. The "Shift Kicker" name would later be used for two unrelated castings in [[Shift Kicker (Convertables)|1991]] and [[Shift Kicker|2004]].

Rumblers:
[[File:Rumblers.png|200px|right]] '''Rumblers''' was a short-lived series of Hot Wheels cars produced from 2007 to 2008. The selling point of the cars was their lights and sound gimmick; as the cars were rolled along, something in the car would flash and light up and rock around (usually an engine) as the cars made noise. Each model features a plastic body; they are slightly bigger than a standard Hot Wheels car and uses three LR44 button cell batteries for the sound effects; a switch on the bottom could be used to lock the rocking function in place, with there being no way to turn off the sounds themselves unless the batteries were removed. Despite being bigger Rumblers cars are compatible with Hot Wheels track. Batteries are not required to play with the cars themselves as the rocking elements are mechanical. Taking the cars apart reveals a cylindrical speaker, a free front axle, a soundboard and a rear axle with small "fingers" on it to key into various functions within the car. When the switch is locked, two pegs are pushed from within the switches to push up onto the rocking object to rock it back and forth as the car is pushed along. A small trigger which the finger keys into at the bottom of the mechanism triggers the car's sound effects and lights; when repeatedly pressed the sound effects are extended. The 2007 castings were reused from the previous Hot Wheels [[Speed Readerz]] line from about 2006, while the 2008 castings were all-new. The series was not successful and none were manufactured after 2008. This series is not to be confused with the [[RRRumblers]] series from the [[Redline]] era. Speed Readerz:
[[File:SpeedReaderz.png|right|200px]]'''Speed Readerz''' was a short-lived series of Hot Wheels cars produced from 2005 to 2006. The selling point of the cars was their speed reading gimmick; the cars could measure their speeds as they rolled along. The cars were packaged in blister packs and could be tried in package with a pull tab. An LCD screen on the cars's roofs would be used to record the speeds. Each of the cars was slightly bigger than a standard Hot Wheels car, but were compatible with Hot Wheels track.

The series was not successful and was discontinued after a year; the series's spiritual successor was the [[Rumblers]] series, with the initial four cars being essentially modified versions of the Speed Readerz vehicles with lights and sounds.

None of the cars had proper names, so placeholder names will be used for their names in this series.

Sizzlers II:
[[File:SizzlersII.png|200px|right]]'''Sizzlers II''' was a successor series to the original [[Sizzlers]] series introduced in 1976. The line introduced six castings, of which only one was actually new, and at least one track set.

All castings were chromed and finished in either silver or gold chrome. The series was particularly short-lived and discontinued in 1978 in favor of the [[Night Ridin' Sizzlers]].

==Description== Released around 2009, the Hot Wheels ''Speed Cycles'' series is a line of miniature motorcycles designed with unique features to enhance both playability and display. What sets these bikes apart from other Hot Wheels vehicles is their specialized base design, which ensures they remain upright without tipping over. Each motorcycle is engineered with a stable, flat base that allows it to stand on its own. The sleek, detailed designs of the bikes often feature bold colors, cool decals, and intricate features that capture the essence of real-world motorcycles, while the stability of their base ensures Speed Chargers:
[[File:SpeedChargers.jpg|200px|right]]'''Speed Chargers''' was a series of motorized vehicles with rechargeable batteries, similar to the [[Sizzlers]] of the 70s or the [[Motorized X-V Racers]] of the 90s; the series was produced from 2016 - 2017. All vehicles in this series were electric themed, taking some preexisting castings and restyling them to be electric, and using some preexisting electric ones. These were exclusive to Target stores. [[Kevin Cao]] was a project lead for this series.

Skate Freaks:
[[File:SkateFreaks.png|200px|right]]'''Skate Freaks''' was a short-lived series of miniature Hot Wheels vehicles produced in 2007. These represented people on skateboards, often featuring names referencing skate tricks. The series was a tie-in with [[wikipedia:Woodward Camp|Woodward Camp]], a sport-themed summer camp based in Pennsylvania, with their branding featured prominently on the products of the line. Development of the series was overseen by [[Dave Sheltman]] who designed the associated launchers and skaters.

About 30 Street Packs and some playsets were produced for the line; skateboarders featured a magnet under them to allow them to stick to the playsets and perform tricks. This concept was also seen on the equally short-lived [[Micro Madnetics]] series but was executed differently.

==Street Packs==
Street Packs were a bundle featuring two skateboarders and a launcher (more akin to that of a pusher), activated by tapping hard on the corrugated portion. The packs could feature repeat models but with different color schemes.

Shogun Racers:
[[File:Sho Gun.JPG|thumb|396px]]
==Description==
'''Shogun Racers''' ''Morphing Tuners™'' is a series of large scale transforming cars released in [[2001]]. Each cars' transformation is suited to racing on a specific type of terrain. Every vehicle came with a manga styled comic and diorama base. Only 6 unique comics were made, later recolors reused the comics from the original releases.

Sky Busters:
[[File:HotWheelsSkyBusters.jpeg|right|300px]]'''Sky Busters'''<ref>[https://m.service.mattel.com/us/Technical/productDetail?prodno=BBL47 Hot Wheels Sky Busters Assortment - Mattel Global Consumer Support]</ref> is an international series of 1/64 scale aircraft that first debuted under [[Hot Wheels]] in [[2013]], designed in conjunction with [[Matchbox]] by [[Mark Jones]], [[Leo Zugner]], and [[Design Team|many others]]. Some graphics were designed by [[Michael Heralda]]. Models were released under the [[HW City Series|HW City]] label until [[2016]]. Some releases began using plastic inserts instead of [[wheel types]] around [[2017]]. Tooling identification numbers are listed on the base of each model near a raised [[Thailand Elephant]]. Toy numbers are listed on packaging. 

All models were released under the [[Matchbox]] brand name and "SB-###" collector number system in the United States.''

==Official Description==
Reach for the stars and become an ace flyer! The Hot Wheels® Sky Busters™ aircraft collection features realistic replicas of airplanes, jets and helicopters that look just like the real thing! Kids and collectors alike will love the incredible detail and awesome decos that inspire epic storytelling and exploration. Whether for play or display, the eye-catching styling of each Hot Wheels® Sky Busters™ aircraft is a sight to behold and perfect to launch a collection. Flight enthusiasts will want to collect them all! Each sold separately, subject to availability. Colors and decorations may vary. The Hot Wheels® Sky Busters™ line of aircraft features 1:64 scale replicas that make for high-flying push-around play and also look great on display. The toy aircraft appeal to both kids and collectors for their awesome detail and design. Each model is a great introduction to the world of 1:64 scale Hot Wheels® aircraft and an essential addition to any aviation enthusiast's collection. The Sky Busters™ line includes jets, planes, and helicopters that will take any collection to new heights -- aviation enthusiasts will want them all (each sold separately, subject to availability)! Kids 3 years old and older fly over any challenges with this awesome toy aircraft that aviation experts will love for its authenticity.

Scorchin' Wheelie:
Released: 2003

Status: Discontinued
[[File:Scorchin wheelie.png|thumb]]
The Scorchin' Wheelie is a motorized vehicle from Hot Wheels' 2003 line of motorized light and sound vehicles. Loosely based on the Muscle Tone, this car has five buttons on it's roof each with different symbols on them. The key button starts the engine, the button with the front of the car on it makes the car shake while idling, the music note plays music, the lightning bolt makes the car shake and the engine to light up and start flashing. A crashing thunder noise is heard followed by a male voice shouting "Hot Wheels!". However, the button with the arrow on it is where the car get's its name, the car will drive off and pop a wheelie when pressed. 
[[File:Scorchin wheelie red .png|thumb|Red version of the Scorchin' Wheelie with additional sounds ]]
Later on in 2003, a red version with flames on the side was released. This version has additional vocal phrases on it, and an additional heavy metal rock tune that plays when the music button is pressed. When the key button is pressed a voice will say "Fire it up!" before the engine starts. The shake button when pressed, will have the voice say "Feel the thunder!" and the engine will rev. The lighting bolt button actually has 2 different phrases "Hot Wheels rules the road!" and "Hot Wheels, it's race time!" before the car starts to shake and the engine lights up and flashes. The wheelie button will make the car say "Stand back, it's wheelie time!" before the car takes off and does a wheelie.

Small Shots:
[[File:SmallShotslogo.png|center|300px]]
==Description==
'''Small Shots''' (later '''Super Small Shots''') is a series of dolls designed by [[Sidney Bass]]<ref>[https://patents.google.com/patent/USD224249S Freely rolling support for figure toy or the like - Pat. USD224249S] </ref> and [[Mando Baeza]]<ref>[https://patents.google.com/patent/US3706155A Jointed figure toy having cooperating bearing surfaces of duplicate size and contours - Pat. US3706155A] </ref> made to function on [[Hot Wheels]] track, released from [[1971]] until [[1973]] with a purpose of introducing girls to [[Hot Wheels]] and boys to high-fashion dolls. It consisted of four removable doll castings fixed on five different connectable stands (Fast Skates, Wagon, Skate Crate, Soapbox Kart, Go Kart) with removable and glued clothing accessories. Some releases included a Skate Ramp track part. Torso and head pieces were rotomolded using LDPE flexible plastic. A commercial advertisement was aired on cable television featuring actor and celebrity Jodie Foster in one of her early roles at roughly 8 years old. Partner company [[Totsy]] created various outfit sets in [[1971]]. Castings were retooled once in [[1973]] with swiveling Action Waists and printed white undergarments. This series alongside many others of the red line era were officially deemed [[Hot Wheels]] products in publications from [[2003]]. 

Some releases of [[1971]] suffer from [[crumbler]] issues.

Steering Rigs:
Hot Wheels [[Steering Rigs]] was a line of detailed semi tractor and trailer sets that were released in 1981 and 1982. On the back of the trailer, there was a large wheel on top which could be used to steer the rig. See detail below:

[[Image:Steering Rig Detail - 7617cf.jpg|200px|left|thumb|Steering wheel detail.]][[File:IMG 6220.JPG|150px]] [[File:IMG 6219.JPG|200px]]

They were produced in two locations: Hong Kong and France. Both pieces will have the country of manufacture on them. The differences between the France and Hong Kong can be very minor (just the base) or significant (colors or opening doors). The French weren't too discerning when putting the tractor and trailer together. There have been several examples where the semi and trailer were mixed up, i.e. a Peterbilt semi with a Allied Moving trailer (should be a Mack semi). In 1982, along with the blue Hong Kong packaging, red packaging was introduced like the French pieces. Another special feature of the Steering Rigs is a piece of rubber on a set of the semi wheels and a set of the trailer wheels, see the following pictures. The rubber is needed to give the wheels grip. Star Wars Character Cars:
The Hot Wheels Star Wars Character Cars lineup have hit the store shelves in October 2014. The cars themselves made their debut at the 2014 San Diego Comic-Con Hot Wheels booth. The cars are designed to represent the most famous characters from the Star Wars series. Every character car has a faction logo on its base, displaying their allegiance to a specific group: Jedi Order, Galactic Republic, Empire, Resistance, Separatist, First Order, Sith... ==Single ==Description==
These iconic Star Wars ships are faithfully recreated by Hot Wheels. They include the finest details and even include a so-called 'Flight Navigator', this is basically a stand for the ship in which you can insert a finger and swoosh the spaceship around. In 2017 the 'Flight Navigator' was replaced by 'Flight Stand', a round base displaying faction logos.
<references />All castings were designed by [[Chris Colangelo]].

Super Mario Character Cars:
Super Mario is a series of platform video games created by Nintendo featuring their mascot, Mario, an Italian plumber. The Super Mario games follow Mario's adventures in the fictional Mushroom Kingdom, usually with Mario as the player character. He is usually joined by his brother, Luigi, and occasionally by other members of the Mario cast. As in platform video games, the player runs and jumps across platforms and atop enemies in themed levels. The games have simple plots, typically with Mario rescuing the kidnapped Princess Peach from the primary antagonist, Bowser. The first title in the series, Super Mario Bros., was released in 1985. The '''Super Mario Character Car series''' features 6 different models that were launched in July 2016. Star Wars Carships:
[[File:B04d286650a4c505736d59aec4e6c694 L.jpg|200px|right]] The Hot Wheels Star Wars Carships lineup have hit the store shelves in October 2016. The cars themselves made their debut at the 2016 San Diego Comic-Con Hot Wheels booth. The cars are designed to represent the most famous starships from the Star Wars series. Star Wars All-Terrain Character Cars:
==Description== These iconic Star Wars character are comically recreated by Hot Wheels. They are 1:43-scale off-road caricatures of famous Star Wars characters. These souped-up cars are related to the regular Character Cars. They have working suspension. The All-Terrain Characters Cars were released in August 2017. "Your favorite ''Star Wars''™ Characters Cars™ are taking it from the streets to any terrain in the galaxy. With an active suspension and larger tires, these reimagined vehicles are designed for off-road domination. Navigating the sandy dunes of Tatooine while on a high-speed chase is no issue for these awesome racers. Encountering the enemy on the snowy fields of Hoth becomes an afterthought as you plow your way through a nasty blizzard. Street Rodder 2-Car Set:
Southern California was a hot-bed of creativity during the early days of street rods and custom cars. Young rebel builders were busy turning old junkers into molded metal dreams. The sounds of souped up engine erupted from backyard garages and cars were being raced everywhere from Van Nuys Boulevard to the Sunset Strip.

Perhaps the most popular cars to customize were Fords. They had great lines, parts were plentiful and they were easy and inexpensive to work on. The result was an outpouring of some of the coolest street rods in history.

Our Hot Wheels Street Rodder car set includes a classic '34 Roadster and a '47 Convertible proudly displayed in a Street Rodder Magazine setting.

Splittin' Images 2-Car Set:
In 2002, [[100% Hot Wheels]] re-released its classic [[Splittin' Image]] with a brand new detailed casting and created a new, modern version. This was the only release of these two castings.

[[File:100SplitBoxFront.JPG|500px]]

Recently several auto makers have successfully produced updated versions of older models. 100% Hot Wheels is out to prove that we can 'go retro' with the best of them with our Splittin' Images set. [[Splittin' Image]] was a concept car designed in 1969 by [[Ira Gilford]], the same year his [[Twin Mill|Twinmill]] debuted. With its futurist styling, twin cockpit canopies and exposed engine, Splittin' Image has been a collector favorite spanning five decades. The vehicle was the perfect choice to be brought into the 21st century with a refined and updated design and emblazoned with a special paint color. It's the way we have updated its 'Image'.

Super Rigs:
[[File:SuperRigs.png|200px|right]]'''Super Rigs''' is the sixth series of transport trucks and included bonus vehicles, coming after [[Long Haulers]], [[Pavement Pounders]], [[Truckin' Transporters]], [[Racing Rigs]], and [[Trackin' Trucks]]. The series started in 2014 and received a logo in 2020. ==2014== First year of the Super Rigs. 6 new models with 2 variations each. All packages had the full blister with City on the side. All models in the Super Rigs line have 2 variations throughout the series, and all models remain unchanged and carry the same Toy # no matter the year. The only thing that changes is the packaging style. Each year will have new models introduced with re-releases from the previous year(s). Speedway Specials:
The '''Speedway Specials''' series was one of seven themes as part of what some call the "Patch Cards".  You could mail in six proofs of purchase and 25 cents for shipping and handling to receive one patch.  These were produced in 1978 and 1979, and all were made in Hong Kong.  Several of these models were also found on the Flying Colors cards.

Stunt Devils:
[[File:Stunt Devils Logo.png|center|thumb|680x680px]] 

'''Stunt Devils''' was a line of Team Hot Wheels specially designed vehicles that could come apart on impact on a surface back in 2012 and 2013. They could easily go back together with just a click. The Stunt Devils are divided in 4 different types. Backflip, Jumper, Spin-Out and Crasher each has there own way to perform stunts, Backflip vehicles use their bottom base to catapult them into the air and by using the base as a center area of gravity they can nail the landing most of the time. 

Spin-Out vehicles had to ability to split their body into a V like shape and spin-out in circles on the ground.

Jumpers have special suspension which could make them jump up in a very high distance.

And Crashers could make there body's look like they suffered a horrendous car wreck. Each vehicle in the series was a variance of a pre-existing vehicle such as Bad to the Blade or Baja Truck and were all classified as [[Team Hot Wheels|HWTF]] vehicles.

==Playset==

=====Stunt Devils Action Arena (2013)=====
''Set Number: BCC95''
[[File:Stunt Devils Action Arena.jpg|thumb|520x520px|The Team Hot Wheels series was wild with there sets!]]
The Stunt Devils Action Arena is a very unique set. The sets primary feature is the large gray base with multiple different stunts to do, these include flying through and take down the flaming hoop, going through a loop and crashing out a breakable wall and doing a jump on the ramp area which features a connection point for track. All these stunts could be accomplished by the modular configuration abilities of the yellow and blue launchers included in the set, these launchers could be moved to different areas on the base to do these respective stunts. The set includes the Stunt Devils version of Fast Fish in green which was exclusive to the set, and was considered apart of the greater Team Hot Wheels toyline and franchise.

[[File:SplitSpeeders.png|200px|right]]'''Split Speeders''' was a short-lived series of Hot Wheels cars produced from 2016 to 2017. These were a gimmicky series of Hot Wheels cars which could split into halves using magnets; this allowed two different halves of cars to come together to create another car. The series was not popular and was quietly discontinued in 2017.

Most of the cars' names invoke the word "split" or some synonym of it.

Stunt Chargers:
'''Stunt Chargers''' was a very short-lived series of Hot Wheels cars produced only in 2013. The selling point of the cars were that you can charge them for 20 seconds in your charge base then when your done you can watch them rebound against walls and ricochet in corners. The vehicles themselves are made in such a way that they can always stay upright. There was only two known cars in this series simply known as [[Car (Stunt Chargers)]] and [[Motorcycle (Stunt Chargers)]] both of which came in a few colors. Due to the toys presuming poor sales they never seen released in future years.

Start Your Engines:
[[File:Start Your Engines.jpg|300px]]

In the 90s, during the height of NASCAR, and near the [[wiki:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Wilkesboro_Speedway|North Wilkesboro Speedway]], a small group of local diecast and NASCAR enthusiast came together to form the Start Your Engine! group. Little is known about this group. But what is know is by joining via mail you would receive a decorative special edition NASCAR and a matching post card. Not only was the NASCAR highly detailed for its time, and the front of the blister decorative to tribute the driver, but the back of the blister has the history and accomplishments of said driver.

The cars came from all brands that where popular at the time such as ERTL, Matchbox, and of course Hot Wheels. But unlike [[Code 3]] cars, as shown on the back of the blister, the group was able to license these cars with Hot Wheels and other related brand in order to produce these cars.

If any more additional info is known about this series, such as members of this group, or what it was like to be part of the group, or when and why did the group disband, please contact [[User:Sval9500|Sval9500]] ([[User talk:Sval9500|talk]]). As a collector locally from this area, I would like to know about the local history, the details of this group, and how collecting was like "back in the good o days". Thanks

Star Wars Starships Select:
[[File:StarshipsSelect png.webp|200px|right]] '''Star Wars Starships Select''' is a line of 1:50 scale replicas of starships from the ''[[wikipedia:Star Wars|Star Wars]]'' media franchise, acting as a sort of Premium version to the standard [[Star Wars Starships|Starships]] line. These versions feature various moving features and are of a larger scale compared to regular Hot Wheels Starships and features an "upgraded" display stand specific to each ship, featuring an etching of the ship's name as well as the logo of its galactic affiliation. Each mix consists of four or five starships; within each mix there includes a single "Chase" variant of one of the four ships with a battle-damaged decoration. These can be identified by the blue background surrounding the name on the packaging (as opposed to silver), a silver background surrounding its series number on the J-hook (as opposed to red) and the series logo reading "'''Starships Select Variant'''" as opposed to simply "Starships Select". {{stub}} [[Image:Super Hot Wheels Logo.PNG|350px]] ==Description== '''Super Hot Wheels''' was an Italian exclusive Hot Wheels line of 1/43 scale die cast cars produced from 1982 to 1985. These used new Mebetoys castings as well as occasional older [[Gran Toros]] castings. The casting have a Hot Wheels base and some Adventure packs series ''("Serie Avventura") ''was made for the series. It is noted that each car came with a sheet of stickers. So any loose version of these cars with different decals might simply be a difference of stickers. It is also debated if the 2 Pack is 2 cars from the Single Car versions of something new entirely. Stretch Racers:
'''Stretch Racers''' was a series of cars released in 2002, they feature a unique play feature: they can extend and be pumped up, then pushed back together and the energy can be released with a push of a button, propelling the car. They are roughly 1:24 scale in size. On [[Alec Tam]]'s personal site it is shown that this series was called ''Shock Racers'' in development.

[[File:Streex Logo.jpg|center|500px]] [[File:Hot Wheels Jet Streex Target Tower - Hot Wheels|center|500px]] ==Description== '''Streex''' was a brief series from [[1992]] that was the "Future of Hot Wheels". These small, plastic ships are really fast on tracks or flat surfaces. They connect to a launcher that is filled with air. When the launcher is pressed, the air pushes the Streex shuttle into action. They where sold in sets with Launchers, 4 Packs, a [[McDonald's#1992 Hot Wheels Streex series|McDonald's series]], or as a sub series known as '''Jet Streex'''. Same concept, but with Jet planes. The vehicles where not given official names, and they do not have wheels. This series was designed by [[Paul Norris]]. Super Minis:
[[File:SuperMinis.jpg|200px|right]]'''Super Minis''' was a very short-lived series of 1/36 scale Hot Wheels models produced around [[1994]] to [[1995]]. These larger scale models were packaged in special packaging with a standing badge showcasing their make. Each model features suspension and opening parts.

The models themselves were actually originally manufactured by Corgi, and feature Corgi branding on their bases; this series was essentially a rebranding of the Corgi series of the same name. This series appears to have only been sold in Europe and some parts of Latin America, particularly Mexico.

Star Wars Battle Rollers:
==Description==
'''Star Wars Battle Rollers''' was a series released from [[2017]]-[[2018]] that featured popular Star Wars Ships and their Pilots on a small cartoonish scale. Each ship had a marble wheel in the center that made them roll towards the enemy and knocking them out. All ships were made by China.

For 2018, the packaging was changed to a yellow blister in honor of the recently released [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solo:_A_Star_Wars_Story Solo: A Star Wars Story]. Some ships came out in either the "Solo Card" or ''The Last Jedi'' card.

Squinkies:
[[File:Squinkdisplay.jpg|center|200px]]
'''Squinkies''' were a toy line from the early 2010s created by '''Blip Toys'''. They were miniature rubber figures of many popular franchises of the time such as Marvel, Disney Princesses, Pixar, WWE and their own original designs.

From 2011 to 2013 Hot Wheels '''Squinkies''' were sold. They featured many of the popular castings from the era in multiple different colors. They were sold in  'Motor Madness' Capsule Packs which featured all 12 cars from whichever 'series' was advertised on the front of the package or they could be found in blind bags which featured two cars from its respectable series.
The Motor Madness packs retailed for around $10 USD and the blind bags retailed for around $3 USD.

'''Shark Attack Tank''' was the only playset introduced as part of this line.

Steerable Wheels:
[[File:SteerableWheelsTranscript.png|center|300px]]
==Description==
'''Steerable Wheels''' is an unreleased series designed by [[Derek Gable]] and [[Design Team|many others]] planned for debut around [[1975]]. It would have featured castings with window cutouts to allow for an extra [[RL]] or [[BW]] wheel type modified into a steering wheel. Several brass base prototypes exist featuring figures and other added components. This series was cancelled due to production costs and track limitations presented by manual operation. Many of these prototypes are on display at the museum operated by licensed author [[Bruce Pascal]] in Maryland.

Team Transporter:
==Description== '''Team Transporters''' was the first series of transport trucks which feature [[Real Riders]]. The series was introduced during the [[1998 Pro Racing]] series and ran until the end of 2005. These were large-scale trucks intended to store NASCAR models inside them. ==Distinguishing the models== Though the cabs are the same with the three different models, there are ways to tell what type of hauler you have without opening the case (Yes, the names are featured on the base of the truck). [[Image:Compare TEAM TRANSPORT.jpg|left|200px]] {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size: 95%; text-align: left;" width="100%" |- |[[Image:International petty.JPG|200px]] |[[International Eagle 9400]] |The easiest to identify, as it is the only hauler out of the three to have the the exhaust stacks in the middle of the truck. |- |[[Image:Kenworth alltel.JPG|200px]] |[[Kenworth T2000]] |The somewhat easy to identify, as the International Eagle and the Kenworth are the two most popular models within the series. Since the exhaust stacks are at the rear it's definitely not an International Eagle. The Kenworth is more smoother and rounder, having circle headlight, instead of boxy headlights. Another easy indicator to identify a Kenworth is to check the window imprint on the wind deflector. The Kenworth's window is the narrowest. |- |[[Image:Frieghtliner cheerios.JPG|200px]] |[[Freightliner Columbia]] |The hardest to identify, as not only is it a rarely used model, but it looks similar to the Kenworth. The main way to identify a Freightliner Columbia is to check the window imprint on the wind deflector. The Freightliner's window is the widest. Top Speed:
[[File:Top 20Speed 20logo.png|200px|right]]
Hot Wheels '''Top Speed''' was a line of futuristic all-plastic vehicles introduced in 1995 and advertised as the "most advanced vehicles in Hot Wheels History!"

Eight unique castings were issued exclusively for Top Speed and each featured a small metal hook on the bottom which could be hooked into a special launcher which was also exclusive to the series. A sub-series called "NEW Solar Flares Vehicles" featured two castings that were exclusive to the Solar Flares series while the other six vehicles could be found in both the Solar Flares sub-series and the regular series. The cars had a chassis bar on the base which could be moved forward to restrict the pivoting body for "drag racing action" and back to release it for "loops, curves and pipes." The cars did not have the name on the base but the names could be found on the rear of the packaging. They were advertised as having "Co-Molded Wheels," a "Floating Front Axle" and a "Poly-Carb Body." Each model came in two "computer-age" color schemes which featured a transparent body, chrome interior and engine piece, brightly colored base, bright tampos and either [[HH|Hot Hubs]] or [[POW|Progressive Oval Wheels]]. The Solar Flares vehicles came with a tinted chrome interior and clear outer portion of the wheels.

The cars could only be purchased in packs of two or included in playsets. The two-packs also included a "Catapult Launcher" and an "Accelerator Tube" of which regular orange track pieces could be connected to. The launcher was to be clipped onto the Accelerator Tube by folding down each end cap of the tube and sliding the launcher onto the end cap ribs. The car was to be placed on the launcher wheels down where the chassis hook drops down freely and the hooked placed into the slot closest to the end of the tube and pulled back until the launcher "clicks" and the starter tab pops out. Press the tab and the car catapults forward at "incredible speed." 

Three playsets were released, the "[[Ultra Pipe Fight]]", "[[Triple Threat]]", and the "[[Cruel Duel]]". The cars were designed by [[Mark Jones]], [[Bruce Baur]], [[Ed Watts]] and [[Paul Norris]].

The bases of each motorcycle is designed in such a way that the bike cannot easily fall over. These bikes have small wheels on either side the motorcycles do not drag on the sidewalls of Hot Wheels tracks. The copyright date for Mattel products is designated a year before, so although the packaging for these bikes may say '2003', for example, it was actually released in 2004. In 2006, the '''Hero Cycles''' line debuted. Then and Now Series:
'''Then and Now''' is a themed line consisting of two different castings of a licensed vehicle, representing a timeline of when the vehicle's first or earlier generation was made, up to the latest generation of the same vehicle. This pair of castings also bear the same paint job and tampo with each other, keeping in line with the timeline theme. The first time Hot Wheels used the name '''Then and Now''' was for an 8 pack in 1995. The next time would be for a stand alone series, [[Batman Vehicles Then and Now]] in 2011. Then in 2013, it was used in the mainline as a sub-segment of the Showroom line. In 2014 and 2015, it was under the mainline segment Workshop. Track Builder:
[[File:TrackBuilder23.png|thumb|Final logo introduced in 2023]]
'''Track Builder''' is a playset line introduced in 2014, initially as part of the Hot Wheels Workshop segment. Each of the playsets featured various stunts and accessories which could be connected together to form numerous track layouts. The line can be seen as a spiritual successor to the [[Track System]] and [[TrackWorx]] lines. Numerous sizes of sets were available, with larger sets containing one or more cars. Bundles of multiple sets were also available. This track system is meant to be all-encompassing; it functions with all previous track systems and cars.

The set received a new logo in 2016 and was also rebranded '''Track Builder System'''. It was given a new stylistic theming, featuring blueprint and construction-like designs elements. Another change noted on the packaging was improved plastic quality. Some boxes also featured perforations which allowed the box to be repurposed into makeshift ramps and obstacles. Track sets also began including [[MEGA Brands]] parts in [[2016]].

With the revamp of the Hot Wheels playset line in 2018, the Track Builder line was added to the ''Growing Up with Hot Wheels'' chart as the final step of the chart. The line was renamed as '''Track Builder Unlimited''' and received a new logo in 2020.  It was restyled with white and blue colors along with stark, industrial theming. Many boxes contained specific components and emphasized the building and rebuilding of different track layouts.

The Track Builder line is also notable for introducing a new type of track connector and track. The connector introduced in 2014 and features small pins that hold two track pieces together and a blue button in the middle which can be pressed to disconnect the track pieces. The new track has a cutout to accommodate the button so the connector sits flush. Older connectors which lack the pin and button can still be used with the new track.

In 2025 the Hot Wheels track system line was completely revamped as [[Track Creator]]. This new line is largely incompatible with all previous track components, though some sets include an adapter which allows Track Creator pieces to be backwards compatible with Track Builder pieces.

TechMods:
[[File:TechMods.png|right|200px]]'''TechMods''' is a series of interactive large-scale remote-controlled cars introduced in 2019. Each car comes unassembled, with the buyer intended to assemble the cars themselves using a wrench, fasteners, ''NeoFlex'' body panels and unique [[TMS|slick tire]]s. The cars can be controlled via a smartphone or similar device and can interact with the phone and the [https://www.youtube.com/shorts/fdBUsvgIoTY Hot Wheels TechMods App]. All cars are powered by a 250mAh lithium-polymer battery, which is included; the battery is charged via a USB port. [[Kevin Cao]] is a lead designer for the series.

The project was funded using [https://www.indiegogo.com/projects/hot-wheels-techmods-accelo-gt#/ Indiegogo], having surpassed its original goal of 400 perks claimed.

Tech Trax:
[[File:TechTrax.png|200x200px|right]]Released in 2004 and 2005, the '''Tech Trax''' series of cars and tracks was a new take on Hot Wheels racing, Featuring cars with articulation and configurable weights, and flexible, highly configurable track. They were designed with creative oversight from [https://www.object8.com/about Object 8].

The cars were released in 2 packs, coming with 1 assembled car and a disassembled car. There were 3 sets released featuring 3 different types of articulation. "Turbo Torque" a central pivot similar to [[XS-IVE]], "Jump Master" a central hinge in the car with a spring attached to keep the car level, and finally the "Power Pivot", a downward facing hinge in the center of the the car, allowing the car to bend in turns. The individual cars did not get names. 

The track system, according to a patent, was designed by [[Dave Sheltman]], [[Mike Finizza]], Joe Pohlman, Mark Mayer, Mike Andrews and Nelson Tam. Scott Shinkle also takes credit for the design of the track on his portfolio.

[[File:The LOYAL SUBJECTS LOS ANGELES HWFlame LOGO.jpg|500px]] ==Description== In the wake of the highly popular collectible toy [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funko Funko Pop], many different brands produced their own form of collectible models consistently style in their unique way starting in the 2010s. Themed assortment:
[[File:SilverSeries.png|right|200px]]"'''Themed assortment'''" is the name given to a sub-segment of the Hot Wheels lineup; products in this series are usually released in sets of five or six models done to a certain theme with similar graphics done to that theme. Slotted above the mainline and below Premium and Red Line Club, vehicles in these series tend to feature enhanced paint and graphics over standard mainline models, with some featuring metal chassis. As of 2023, the vehicles in these series typically use specially designed plastic wheels. These can be identified by their silver Hot Wheels logos on their cards; this series is advertised as "Silver Label".

The series was officially named '''Silver Series''' in [[2025]].

Track Creator:
[[File:TrackCreator.png|right|200px]]
'''Track Creator''' is a playset line that launched in 2025 as a replacement to the previous [[Track Builder]] system.

It introduces a new type of connector system, named the ''[[Speed Snap]]'' system, which uses a peg-and-socket system to allow for easier assembly; this type of connector is incompatible with previous connectors and track components.  Some sets include an adapter which allows Track Creator pieces to be backwards compatible with Track Builder pieces. This Speed Snap system also replaced Track Builder style connectors on [[Hot Wheels City]] sets.

Treasure Hunt:
[[File:RaijinHauler.jpg|200px|right|thumb|A typical modern Treasure Hunt, the [[Raijin Express]] from 2023.]][[File:RTH.png|200px|right|thumb|The logo used since [[2013]] to identify Treasure Hunts.]]"'''Treasure Hunt'''" (often abbreviated as '''TH''') is a term used by Mattel to refer to a number of intentionally-production limited Hot Wheels placed within the mainline.

Hot Wheels introduced the [[1995 Treasure Hunts Series|Treasure Hunts series]] in [[1995]], featuring a series of twelve vehicles; each vehicle was only produced in 10,000 examples. These series could be identified by a green bar with the series name and icon within them. This quantity was increased to 25,000 in 1996 before the production quantity was removed from 1997 onwards. Treasure Hunts from 1997 to 2006 featured special wheels (usually [[Real Riders]] or something of that sort); later Treasure Hunts featured a logo (usually some variation on the letters "TH") to identify them.

From 2007, a two-tiered system was introduced; while the Treasure Hunt series was retained, new highly-collectible versions of the standard Treasure Hunts were introduced; these were stylized as "TREA$URE HUNT$" on the package and are most commonly referred to as "[[Super Treasure Hunt]]s". The Treasure Hunts series continued until 2012, while the Super Treasure Hunts were spun off into a "hidden" series in 2012 within the mainline, with random vehicles within the standard mainline segment given the Super Treasure Hunt treatment.

Since 2013, Treasure Hunts have also been made a "hidden" series, with random vehicles within the standard mainline segments being made Treasure Hunts. These are identified by a symbol as shown above, commonly referred to as "the circle flame logo". The same logo is also printed on the card backs of these models; US cards feature a congratulatory message. Similar logos have also been used in the [[Hot Wheels Monster Trucks]] series since 2021 and the [[Hot Wheels Skate]] series since 2022. The term "Regular Treasure Hunt" (often abbreviated RTH) has since sprung into recent use to differentiate these from the more collectible Super Treasure Hunts.

==Trivia==
*A full Hot Wheels case of 72 cars will typically feature exactly one Treasure Hunt; cases without a Treasure Hunt are rare but they do exist.
*The presence of the "circle flame" logo on a casting after 2013 does not mean that the casting is a Treasure Hunt; this logo only has meaning if it is within the mainline and the logo's presence in other series means nothing as these series tend to reuse older tampos on occasion, and prior to 2013, that logo meant nothing.
*Combining both the standard and Super Treasure Hunts, the [['57 Chevy]] has been used the most often, appearing six times.
*The [[2015]] release of the [[Fiat 500]] has the Treasure Hunt symbol (and associated congratulatory message) printed on the card back in error.

Turbo Driver:
{{casting|name=Turbo Driver|series=|number=N1709|years=2008|designer=|image=TDinpackage.jpg}}

The [[HotWheels.com]] '''Turbo Driver''' is an online computer game controller that gives players access to the [[Race The World]] computer game, as well as more than 20 cool games hosted on HotWheels.com.

There are eight different [[Car-tridge]] vehicles created exclusively for the controller, and the Car-tridge you plug into the controller is the same car that you play in the exclusive Race The World game. When you change the Car-tridge™ in the controller, the car automatically changes on the screen.

Plus, the controller can be used to play over 20 games on HotWheels.com and will be compatible with future games launched there.

On January 1st, 2010, the online servers were shut down for unknown reasons.

==Race The World Game==
Race The World gives the player the chance to race in eight different worlds, each with its own terrain and unique obstacles. Each car has a secret ability that gives it the best performance in its home world and all of the cars perform slightly differently in each world. So, no matter which car you race, there are always new things to find. If that weren’t enough, when you beat all eight worlds, the player unlock the secret ninth world!

Track Stars:
Originally called [[Track Aces]], '''Track Stars''' are a group of castings that perform exceptionally well on most [[Hot Wheels]] track and playsets. Typically, '''Track Stars''' are released with plastic bodies and a metal [[chassis]] to give them a lower center of gravity making them "stick" to the track all the better. In 2008 [[Hot Wheels Trick Tracks]] were released. Since about 2014 packages of castings indicate track star status on cars not in the series. Since 2020, the cars now feature bright orange tires, and the packages of single die casts feature the car running on the iconic orange track. The "Track Stars" name was dropped for 2022 onwards, being replaced by the [[HW Speed Team Mini Collection (2022)|HW Speed Team]] segment for 2022 and the [[HW Track Champs Mini Collection (2023)|HW Track Champs]] segment for 2023 and 2024. The "Track Stars" name is still however used to signify a car's good performance on track in the international market. Vintage Series:
[[File:Otto Vintage Series.png|center|750px]] [[Vintage Series]] was a special set of cars that were issued after the popular [[25th Anniversary Series|25th Anniversary]] cars. Appearing in [[1993]] to [[1994]] they were reissued copies of some of the [[Original 16]] cars and other early Hot Wheels castings. Just like the [[Original 16]], each car came with many colorful variations, but in metallic paint, not Spectraflame. Each car came packaged in a replica 1968 blister with a replica plastic [[Collector's Button]]. They also appeared in three different blisters: '''25th Anniversary''' which has 25th Anniversary on the left top corner. [[File:Red Baron-25th Bright Red.jpg|200px]] '''Vintage Series''' is a normal card with "Vintage Collection" in the top left corner. [[File:1993_Vintage_Series_II_Button_Blister_Card_Snake.jpg|200px]] '''Vintage Series II''' is almost like the Vintage Series card but on "Exclusive Series II" on the right side. Vintage Series II was exclusive to only Toys 'r' Us stores. Tri Five Chevy 3-Car Set:
[[File:Tri Five Chevy 3-Car Set.JPG|750px]]

During the mid fifties no one could match Chevrolet in capturing the hearts and minds car buyers with clean, sporty designs. During an era in which body styles changed annually, the Chevy designers produced classic after classic. The '55 Bel Air broke new ground with its sleek lines and legendary small block V-8, the '56 kept sale soaring, and what can be written about the '57 Nomad that you haven't read a million times. It was the ultimate in 50s design.

These cars have been named the Tri-Fives and 100% Hot Wheels is proud to produce this classy and classic 3 car set.

Woodward Ave. 2-Car Set:
[[File:WoodwardAveBoxFront.JPG|500px]]

Detroit's Woodward Avenue has been a mecca for Motor City cruisin' for five decades. In the '50's it was a few lowered cars with whitewall tires, skirts and spinners - nowadays it's the site of an annual reunion that attracts rod and custom car enthusiasts from across the country. But it was during the mid '60's when Woodward's repuation grew to legendary status. The car culture changed from 'Low and Slow' to 'Fast Forward'. With the sounds of Motwon music blaring from car radios, early muscle machines mingled with the city's hottest rods and coolect customs in a nightly ritual of cruisin' to the north end of Woodward. There, Ted's Drive-In offered hot burgers, cool waitresses and the chance for engine revvin', clutch poppin', tire screechin', and stoplight-to-stoplight street racin'. Those were 'the days' and Hot Wheels Woodward Avenue 2-Car Set can take you back there.

Vintage Pony Wars Road Racing 2-Car Sets:
Originated in 1966 by the Sports Car Club of America, it was officially known as the Trans-American Sedan Series, but to the legions of racing fans who loved watching America's most popular drivers behind the wheels of the country's most popular muscle cars, it was simply referred to as 'Trans-Am'.

For the next six years each Trans-Am event would prove to be a battle in the ongoing Pony Car wars. These bumper-bangin' races were held on the country's most challenging road courses such as Sebring and Watkin's Glen, and established the annual Manufacturer's Championship.

Troy Lee Designs:
Troy Lee Designs is a action sports apparel and custom paint company founded in [[1981]] by Troy Lee, a former motocross racer and grandson of Bonneville Speed Trials co-founder Marvin Lee. While primarily focused on custom motocross apparel and helmets, TLD has expanded into other designs ventures including the custom artwork on the vehicles from ''The Fast and The Furious'' (2001) film and several [[Hot Wheels]] vehicles.

Voodoo Highway 3-Car Set:
[[Image:Voodoo Highway 3-Car Set.JPG|750px]]

To custom car fanatics "cruisin" has become a weekly routine, but to the practitioners of the mystical and magical the ritual goes far beyond a Friday night spin to the hot dog stand. To the tricksters of Voodoo Highway, driving around like a zombie in anything less than the coolest of custom cars is an insult to the spirits of the two-lane asphalt.

Now, you too may become bewitched by the boulevard before you. The high priests of design at [[100% Hot Wheels|Hot Wheels Collectibles]] have conjured a spellbinding set of vehicles with super-natural graphics and super-charged engines, known as Voodoo Highway. So, hang your harlequin doll and qris-qris bag on your rear view mirror and take a mystical and magical trip down a road less travelled... Voodoo Highway.

Turbo Glo:
[[File:TurboGlo Logo.png|right|200x200px]]
'''Turbo Glo ''' was a series of Hot Wheels from 2006, one series in a long line of successors to the original [[Sizzlers]]. Turbo Glo cars were motorized and charged on a separate charger included with each vehicle. Similar to the [[Motorized X-V Racers#Light Speeders|Motorized X-V Racers: ''Light Speeders'']] they featured clear bases with lights emulating underglow lights which were a popular modification for real cars at the time. All cars in the series were based on mainline casting designs including [[Bully Goat]], [[Symbolic]], [[Asphalt Assault]], and the [[Ferrari FXX]] (although unlicensed). In development this series was called "Street-Glo".

Virtual Garage:
[[File:VirtualGarage.png|200px|right]]'''Virtual Garage''' (named '''NFT Garage''' until 2024) is a Hot Wheels series introduced in [[2022]]. Users of the platform may [https://hotwheelsnftg.io/ purchase] [[wikipedia:Non-fungible token|non-fungible token]]s (NFT) [https://wax.atomichub.io/explorer/collection/hotwheels of Hot] [https://creations.mattel.com/collections/catalog Wheels cars] in packs of between three cars and ten. NFTs are divided into five rarities: Base, Rare, Premium, NFTH and Showroom, with those who receive Premium or NFTH rarity cars from these packs being able to redeem them for physical Hot Wheels models using a "redemption token". The series initially ran on the Worldwide Asset Exchange (WAX) platform before switching to Flow beginning with Series 4. The line was discontinued after Series 10.

Tunerz:
'''Tunerz''' was a series of 1:18 scale tuner cars including extra body kits and wheels for customization. The series started as a part of the [[100% Hot Wheels 1:18 Scale]] line, but the 100% branding was dropped after 2004. 

==Official Production Description==
Featuring four of the coolest tuner cars in the market. Customize
these popular 1:18 tuner die-cast models with replacement rims
and tires, attach a new wing or swap out the spoiler and
change the ground effects. It’s all up to the collector.

X-Raycers:
The first cars produced with transparent bodies appeared in the [[List_of_1997_Hot_Wheels#Phantom_Racer_Series|1997 Phantom Racer Series]]. [[:Category:X-Raycers|X-Raycers]] did not debut as a segment until the 2005 First Editions subset/segment. Since then, they have been available in Mainline cards and 5-Packs. On the following list, the terms "clear", "transparent" or "translucent" all denote the same see-through characteristics of the plastic body. At least one of these cars; the Bullet Proof, was originally made using the technique known as co-molding. Zowees:
[[File:Zowees.png|300px|right]]'''Zowees''' were a series of very small (1/125 scale) Hot Wheels vehicles produced in 1972. There were 8 different vehicles which were originally made for [[Gas Station Promotionals|Shell Oil Company]] as a promotional item which one would receive after fueling up their car, or they could be purchased from the station for $0.49; these were packaged in baggies. After the promotion for Shell, slightly different versions of the original eight and an additional six new vehicles were released and were only available through retail shops. Zowees were made up of a metal piece which was the base and engine, to which the plastic body and wheels would clip in to. At retail shops, Zowees were only packed in multipacks and not available singly. Zowees were available in multipacks featuring two, three, four or even six Zowees. A pack also exists where a car from Hot Wheels's [[List of 1972 Hot Wheels|1972 lineup]] would be packaged with a single Zowees model. Each pack could have duplicates of a single type of Zowees model. The eight Shell promotion Zowees were also sold in Germany by Mattel's German branch, under the name of '''Fun Buggies'''; all eight were given different names. They were advertised with standard Hot Wheels, [[RRRumblers]] and [[Hot Shots]] models, with their slogan being "Die Lustigsten Miniaturautos der Welt" (lit. Zip Rippers:
[[File:Zip Rippers Logo.jpeg|center|thumb|200x200px|The Zip Rippers logo]]
'''Zip Rippers''' was a line of three-wheeled 1:64 scaled Hot Wheels vehicles who's main gimmick was each vehicle having a ripcord that could be used with the vehicle to push them off at powerful speeds. The line which was under the [[HW RACE]] banner lasted from [[2015]] to [[2016]] and was quietly discontinued after it's two year run, most likely due to poor sales and distribution.

== Vehicle Characteristics ==
[[File:Zip Rippers Vehicles.jpeg|thumb|380x380px|Many vehicles from the line.]]
The main characteristics of Zip Ripper vehicles was their massive single back rubber wheel that was almost the size of [[Monster Jam|Monster Truck]] wheels from the time. These wheels where the ones that activate during the time the ripcord is pulled from the vehicle in question, the two front wheels where one of the most early examples of the skinny [[HSRW]] wheel type being used in a HW toyline most likely due to the wheel making vehicles much faster then vehicles with wheels of normal thickness.

Each Vehicle from the line had a hole area where the ripcord could be place on the left side in the vehicle and with a simple strong pull the vehicle in question would activate the play feature that the line of known for.

== Toyline ==
The Zip Rippers toyline compared to others of it's magnitude was a medium size line with one set, one launcher and 6 different new castings, three of them being Zip Ripper variants of well known Hot Wheels thus making Muscle Mania, Haulin' Horsepower  and Rip Roarin (who could be seen as the mascot of the line) the only brand new vehicles added to the vast HW universe.

==== Track Set ====
{{Casting|name=Rip Up Raceway|series=Zip Rippers|years=2015 only|number=CDF30|image=Rip Up Raceway.webp}}
The '''Rip Up Raceway''' was a medium sized straight trackset which was only released in 2015. The set was very simple with having three obstacles the vehicle must go through being a single loop, adjustable jump and a specialized track piece that was meant to represent the vehicle ripping up the pavement road. This was done via switches on the piece that triggers the action. The set was list under the HW RACE banner during it's short time of store shelves and could connect to sets with Track Builder connection points. This was also notable for being one of the first sets to use orange tall wall track pieces.

Vehicles Include:  [[Rip Roarin|Rip Roarin or]] [[Bad to the Blade]]

==== Launcher ====
{{Casting|name=Super Kick Launcher|series=Zip Rippers|years=2016 only|image=Super Kick Launcher.jpg|number=Unknown}}
The '''Super Kick Launcher''' is a unique launcher which features a sloped angled ramp-like track area supported by a yellow handle. The gray area could have a vehicle loaded into to be launched by the launcher's mechanism. The Launcher could be added on to other Hot Wheels track pieces.

Vehicles Include: [[Twin Mill (Zip Rippers)|Twin Mill]]
